before.title: Affine spaces over a real vector space and displacement vectors
before.statement: Let V be a real vector space. An affine space over V is a nonempty set A together with a map +: A x V -> A such that (a) (p+v)+w = p+(v+w) and p+0 = p for all p in A and v,w in V, and (b) for all p,q in A there is exactly one v in V with p+v = q. That unique v is written q-p and called the displacement from p to q. Then p+(q-p) = q, p-p = 0, p+0 = p, (q-p)+(r-q) = r-p, and for each p in A the map v |-> p+v is a bijection A -> A. If V is 4-dimensional and E: R^4 -> V is a linear isomorphism, then x(p) := E^{-1}(p-o) is a bijection A -> R^4 for each o in A; such maps are the affine coordinate systems on A.
before.strategy: The uniqueness clause (b) is what makes q-p well defined. The identities follow from the action axioms and uniqueness: p+(q-p) = q is the defining property of q-p; p-p = 0 and p+0 = p come from p+0 = p; and p+[(q-p)+(r-q)] = [p+(q-p)]+(r-q) = q+(r-q) = r = p+(r-p) gives (q-p)+(r-q) = r-p by uniqueness. For each p, v |-> p+v is surjective by (b) and injective because an equality p+v = p+w and the action axioms give p+(v-w) = p = p+0, so v-w = 0 by (b) applied at (p,p).

references.title: D. Margalit and J. Rabinoff, Interactive Linear Algebra, section 2.7 (affine subspaces and coordinates)
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 pp. 2-7 (PDF pp. 9-14)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), sections 2.1-2.2 pp. 25-28 (PDF pp. 26-29); Internet Archive copy of the original https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/hsr1000/part3_gr_lectures.pdf

before.title: The metric pairing is an isomorphism to the dual, and the raised covector in an orthonormal frame
before.statement: Let (V,eta) be a 4-dimensional Lorentz vector space (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia): eta is symmetric and bilinear, nondegenerate in the sense that both radicals are {0} (def-matrix-radicals-rank-and-nondegeneracy-of-a-bilinear-form), and of inertia (3,1,0). Let V* be the algebraic dual (def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional). Then: (a) the map iota: V -> V*, iota(v)(w) := eta(v,w), is linear and injective, since iota(v) = 0 means eta(v,w) = 0 for all w in V, i.e. v lies in the left radical, which is {0}. (b) dim V* = dim V = 4, so iota is a linear bijection (rank-nullity, thm-rank-nullity). (c) Consequently for every covector k in V* there is a unique vector k^sharp in V with eta(k^sharp,w) = k(w) for all w in V; the assignment sharp: V* -> V, k |-> k^sharp, is linear and is the inverse of iota, so (v^flat)^sharp = v for v^flat := iota(v) and (k^sharp)^flat = k for every k; in particular k^sharp = 0 if and only if k = 0. (d) If (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) is an eta-orthonormal ordered basis of V (lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis) and k_a := k(e_a) are the components of k in it, then k^sharp = -k_0 e_0 + k_1 e_1 + k_2 e_2 + k_3 e_3; that is, in this basis (k^sharp)^0 = -k_0 and (k^sharp)^i = k_i for i = 1,2,3, and eta(k^sharp,k^sharp) = -(k_0)^2 + (k_1)^2 + (k_2)^2 + (k_3)^2. Hence k^sharp is null exactly when (k_0)^2 = (k_1)^2 + (k_2)^2 + (k_3)^2, timelike when the left side is smaller, and spacelike when it is larger (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors). No orientation, time orientation or affine structure is used, and no choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Proof strategy. (a) Linearity in v is the bilinearity of eta; iota(v) = 0 is the statement that v lies in the left radical, and the defining nondegeneracy clause says the left radical is {0}. (b) The dual basis theorem (thm-dual-family-is-a-basis-in-finite-dimension) exhibits a basis of V* with one element per basis element of V, so dim V* = dim V; an injective linear map between finite-dimensional spaces of equal dimension is bijective, either directly by thm-rank-nullity (nullity 0 forces rank = dim V = dim V*) or by the equivalent characterization of invertibility. (c) Surjectivity supplies existence, injectivity supplies uniqueness, and the two inverse identities are immediate from the definitions. (d) Evaluate eta(-k_0 e_0 + sum_i k_i e_i, e_b) using eta-orthonormality: eta(-k_0 e_0, e_0) = -k_0 eta(e_0,e_0) = -k_0(-1) = k_0 and eta(k_i e_i, e_i) = k_i (no summation), with all cross terms zero; this equals k_b on the basis, hence the covectors agree by linearity, giving the component formula. The quadratic form is the diagonal evaluation diag(-1,1,1,1); the causal trichotomy is the definition of causal character. The statement is pure algebra of the Lorentz form and asserts nothing physical. No choice principle is used.

references.title: B. Crowell, Special Relativity, revision 2020-12-10 (author-published undergraduate textbook, 246 PDF pages): Section 3.2 'The stretch factor is the Doppler shift' pp. 55-57, Section 3.3 'Combination of velocities' pp. 57-59, Section 6.4 'Duality' pp. 134-137 (the frequency covector and its dual), Section 6.5.1 'Doppler shift' p. 137, Section 6.5.2 'Aberration' pp. 137-139 and Section 6.6.1 'Phase velocity' pp. 140-141; signature (+---) converted to (-+++) and c = 1 formulas converted to x^0 = c t

before.title: Surface distributions and interfacial jumps
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$, and put $\delta_S(\psi):=\int_S\psi\,dS$ for $\psi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, the surface integral being that of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]. A continuous density $a$ on $S$ defines $a\delta_S(\psi)=\int_S a\psi\,dS$. Both functionals are continuous of finite order on test functions, because $\lvert a\rvert$ and $\psi$ are bounded on the compact interface and the surface measure is finite. A field that is $C^1$ on $\Omega_-\cup\Omega_+$ with one-sided continuous traces has locally integrable components; write $[F]:=F_+-F_-$ for the jump across $S$.
before.strategy: Use the compact surface integral definition and the finite-order estimate for continuous densities; for non-compact interfaces localize with a compactly supported test. The jump $[F]$ is the one-sided trace difference, and the sign convention of $n$ (minus to plus) is fixed here and used by the interface-derivative lemma.

references.title: S. Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (MIT, 2026), Chapter 2 and Chapter 3
J. K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (UC Davis, 2014), §1.10, §1.12, §2.7

after.title: Surface distributions and interfacial jumps
after.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$, and put $\delta_S(\psi):=\int_S\psi\,dS$ for $\psi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, the surface integral being that of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]. A continuous density $a$ on $S$ defines $a\delta_S(\psi)=\int_S a\psi\,dS$. Both functionals are continuous of finite order on test functions, because $\lvert a\rvert$ and $\psi$ are bounded on the compact interface and the surface measure is finite. A field that is $C^1$ on $\Omega_-\cup\Omega_+$ with one-sided continuous traces has locally integrable components; write $[F]:=F_+-F_-$ for the jump across $S$. The compact branch also localizes to a noncompact two-sided embedded $C^2$ interface that is closed in $\Omega$ (equivalently its inclusion is proper): for every compact test support $K$, $S\cap K$ is compact and admits finitely many regular graph patches. Its area integrals use the same compact Borel-face chart formula and finite ambient partition, not an assumed finite total area. If $\Omega\setminus S=\Omega_-\cup\Omega_+$ with both sides open and disjoint, this geometry already makes $S$ relatively closed. More generally, given a compatible chart-area measure on a possibly nonproper interface, a measurable density $a$ defines the weighted pairing directly whenever $\int_{S\cap K}|a|\,dS<\infty$ for every compact ambient $K$; the unweighted pairing requires this condition for $a=1$. No mere embeddedness or compactness of the test alone implies local mass finiteness. An ordinary continuous one-sided trace means an actual continuous extension of the field values to the closed side, locally near the interface; it is not an unspecified weak trace and does not imply integrability of classical derivatives. Such values are locally bounded, hence the fields are locally integrable in the compact/proper geometry. A one-sided $C^1$ extension additionally extends the first derivatives; this stronger condition is distinguished in [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]].
after.strategy: For a compact test support K and proper S, cover S intersect K by finitely many regular graph charts and split a neighbourhood of that compact set with [[lem-finite-ambient-partitions-for-euclidean-boundary-integration]]. The compact Borel-face clause of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]] applies in every chart; overlap and partition independence are exactly [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]. In each chart the Gram density is bounded on the compact parameter support, so finitely many terms give finite area and finite mass for a continuous density. The bound |T_a(psi)|<=sup_K|psi| times the finite integral of |a| on S intersect K proves order-zero continuity by [[thm-local-finite-order-characterization-of-distributions]]. The same estimate proves the conditional measurable-density branch when its local absolute mass is supplied, without asserting that an arbitrary nonproper embedding has it. The integral a delta_S there denotes the weighted pairing, not multiplication of an arbitrary distribution by a nonsmooth function. Ordinary continuous extensions of the values are bounded on each compact closed half-chart; off S use continuity, giving finite local bounds after a finite cover. Set [F]=F_+-F_- with the chosen minus-to-plus normal; extending values alone says nothing about first-derivative integrability.

references.title: S. Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (MIT, 2026), Chapter 2 and Chapter 3
J. K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (UC Davis, 2014), §1.10, §1.12, §2.7

before.title: Localization: vanishing integrals or fluxes force a continuous function to vanish
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and $g:U\to\mathbb R^m$ continuous. If $\int_Vg=0$ for every ball $V$ compactly contained in $U$, then $g=0$ on $U$. Moreover, if $F:U\to\mathbb R^3$ is continuous and the flux of $F$ through every planar disk in each of the three coordinate planes, of every radius for which the closed disk lies in $U$, is zero, then $F=0$ on $U$.
before.strategy: If $g(p)_i>0$, continuity gives a ball $V\Subset U$ on which $g_i\ge g_i(p)/2$; then $0<(g_i(p)/2)\lambda(V)\le\int_Vg_i$, contradicting the hypothesis. Apply to each component and to $-g_i$. The disk statement applies the planar case to each coordinate component with the coordinate normal. One special loop or box does not suffice.

references.title: J. K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (UC Davis, 2014), §1.10, §1.12, §2.7
J. Lebl, Basic Analysis II, §9.1 (Leibniz integral rule), Theorem 9.1.1

after.title: Localization: vanishing integrals or fluxes force a continuous function to vanish
after.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and $g:U\to\mathbb R^m$ continuous. If $\int_Vg=0$ for every ball $V$ compactly contained in $U$, then $g=0$ on $U$. Moreover, in dimension $n=3$, if $F:U\to\mathbb R^3$ is continuous and its flux through every disk of arbitrary center in every translated plane parallel to each of the three coordinate planes, with either fixed coordinate unit normal and every positive radius whose closed disk lies in $U$, is zero, then $F=0$ on $U$.
after.strategy: If $g(p)_i>0$, continuity gives a ball $V\Subset U$ on which $g_i\ge g_i(p)/2$; then $0<(g_i(p)/2)\lambda(V)\le\int_Vg_i$, contradicting the hypothesis. Apply to each component and to $-g_i$. For the disk statement fix p in U and a coordinate normal e_i. The affine plane through p perpendicular to e_i has a small closed disk centered at p contained in U. Its translated linear parameterization is regular and its area Jacobian is one, so the actual surface-flux definition identifies its flux with the two-dimensional Lebesgue integral of F_i on that disk. If F_i(p) has nonzero sign, continuity gives a smaller disk where its absolute value is bounded below by |F_i(p)|/2, and positive disk area gives a contradiction exactly as in the ball argument. Do this for i=1,2,3; disks only in the three origin planes would not suffice (F=(x_1 x_2 x_3,0,0) vanishes there). The general n-dimensional ball statement is unchanged and uses its own measurable-ball hypothesis, not a fixed physical test geometry. One special loop or box does not suffice. The disk parameter domain is the closed disk D_r centered at zero, with r>0: [[cor-disc-jordan-content-is-pi-r-squared]] supplies its compact Jordan measurability and positive content. The affine parameterization (u,v) to p+u e_j+v e_k is defined on all R2, injective, with constant nonzero cross product, so it satisfies the exact admissible regular-patch contract. The Riemann flux integral equals its two-dimensional Lebesgue value by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] applied to the continuous disk integrand and bounded zero extension to a rectangle. This justifies the comparison used above without importing physical fixed-test restrictions into the pure mathematical statement.

references.title: J. K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (UC Davis, 2014), §1.10, §1.12, §2.7
J. Lebl, Basic Analysis II, §9.1 (Leibniz integral rule), Theorem 9.1.1

before.title: Zonal and quadratic sphere moments for the polar surface measure on $S^2$
before.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the dipole and emitted-power items (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-36.notes.md)
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), as carried by the surface-measure interface below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on the unit sphere $S^2\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]), let $e_3:=(0,0,1)$ be the third coordinate unit vector and write $n_3=n\cdot e_3$ for $n\in S^2$. Then: (a) [Zonal identity] for every continuous $f:[-1,1]\to\mathbb R$, $$\int_{S^2}f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}f(u)\,du.$$ (b) [Linear weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)\,f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3\int_{-1}^{1}u\,f(u)\,du.$$ (c) [Quadratic weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3^{2}\int_{-1}^{1}u^{2}f(u)\,du+\pi\,(a_1^{2}+a_2^{2})\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})f(u)\,du.$$ (d) [Moments] $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$, $\int_{S^2}n\,d\sigma=0$, $\int_{S^2}n_in_j\,d\sigma=(4\pi/3)\delta_{ij}$, and for every $a\in\mathbb R^3$ $\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=(4\pi/3)|a|^2$ and $\int_{S^2}|n\times a|^2d\sigma=(8\pi/3)|a|^2$, where $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker symbol and $\times$ the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (e) [Scope] (a)-(d) are identities for the polar surface measure of the unit sphere with only the stated continuity of $f$; they assert no physical field, flux or radiation statement. The measure is finite, so all displayed integrals are absolutely convergent; $f$ need not be nonnegative. For the uses on this page $f$ is a rational function with denominator bounded below by $1-b>0$, hence continuous on $[-1,1]$.
before.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) Parametrize $S^2$ by $X(\theta,\varphi):=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta)$ on $[0,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$. Computing the coordinate cross product with the sin/cos derivatives and the Pythagorean identity ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) gives $X_\theta\times X_\varphi=\sin\theta\,X(\theta,\varphi)$, whose norm is $\sin\theta\ge0$; by [[thm-surface-area-density-is-cross-product-norm]] and [[def-surface-area-and-scalar-surface-integral-of-a-patch]] the chart surface integral of $F(n)=f(n_3)$ is $\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\pi}f(\cos\theta)\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi$, with the seam and the poles lying on the parameter boundary exactly as in the sphere-area computation, so this is the integral over $S^2$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-parameter-boundary-exceptions-do-not-affect-surface-integrals|the boundary-exception convention]]). The chart measure equals the polar measure $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). By [[thm-jordan-fubini-by-sections]] the $\varphi$-integral is the constant $2\pi$, and with $P(u):=\int_0^u f$ ([[thm-ftc-first-part]]) the chain rule and [[thm-ftc-second-part]] give $\int_0^{\pi}f(\cos\theta)\sin\theta\,d\theta=[-P(\cos\theta)]_0^{\pi}=P(1)-P(-1)=\int_{-1}^{1}f(u)\,du$, using $\cos0=1$, $\cos\pi=-1$ and the derivative $\cos'=-\sin$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]]). after.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), as carried by the surface-measure interface below ([[def-countable-choice]]). before.title: Distributional divergence and curl across a stationary interface
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, let $S\subset\Omega$ be a two-sided compact embedded $C^2$ interface with unit normal $n$ from $\Omega_-$ to $\Omega_+$, and let $F$ be $C^1$ on $\Omega_-\cup\Omega_+$ with one-sided $C^1$ traces on $S$. Then, away from the edge $\partial S$ and in the distributional sense, $$\operatorname{div}F=\{\operatorname{div}F\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\cdot[F]\,\delta_S,\qquad \operatorname{curl}F=\{\operatorname{curl}F\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\times[F]\,\delta_S,$$ where the bracket terms denote the locally integrable functions equal to the classical divergence and curl on each open side and $[F]=F_+-F_-$.
before.strategy: Against a test supported away from the edge, split $-\int F\cdot\nabla\psi$ into the two sides and apply the divergence theorem to $\psi F$ on each side; the outward normal is $n$ on the minus side and $-n$ on the plus side, so the boundary terms combine to $(F_+-F_-)\cdot n$. Componentwise integration by parts gives $\partial_iF_j=\{\partial_iF_j\}+n_i[F_j]\delta_S$, and antisymmetrizing the index pair gives the curl formula. A moving interface needs a separate account.

after.title: Distributional divergence and curl across a stationary interface
after.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $S$ be a two-sided compact embedded $C^2$ interface with unit normal $n$ from minus to plus. The same local conclusions hold for an interface closed in $\Omega$, with tests supported away from any edge. Let $F$ be $C^1$ on the open sides and have ordinary continuous extensions of its values to each closed side near $S$, as in [[def-em-surface-distribution]]. For each component there is a canonical bulk distribution $\mathcal B_{ij}$, equal to the classical $\partial_iF_j$ away from $S$, such that $$\partial_iT_{F_j}=\mathcal B_{ij}+n_i[F_j]\delta_S.$$ Thus $\operatorname{div}T_F=\sum_i\mathcal B_{ii}+n\cdot[F]\delta_S$ and $(\operatorname{curl}T_F)_k=\sum_{i,j}\epsilon_{kij}\mathcal B_{ij}+(n\times[F])_k\delta_S$. The bulk distribution is the graph-truncated classical-derivative limit specified below; it need not be a regular locally integrable function. If the piecewise classical first derivatives are locally absolutely integrable across $S$, then $\mathcal B_{ij}=T_{\{\partial_iF_j\}_{\rm piecewise}}$, giving the original regular-bulk divergence and curl identities. In particular this regular specialization applies when the field and its first derivatives have one-sided $C^1$ extensions to the closed sides. Continuous trace values alone are not that stronger hypothesis. No moving-interface formula is asserted.
after.strategy: Fix a compact test supported away from edges. Properness makes its interface intersection compact; use the finite ambient partition to reduce to finitely many graph cylinders, plus interior patches. For a graph z=g(y), trim the sides at z=g(y)-epsilon and z=g(y)+epsilon, keeping the localized test zero near the cylinder's other faces. On each trimmed finite piecewise C1 domain the field is C1 on its compact closure, so [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] applies to psi F_j e_i. It gives the classical derivative integral as minus the F_j derivative-of-test integral minus its outward boundary integral. The two graph faces have the same Gram density and normals tending to n and -n; ordinary continuous value extensions give uniform convergence on the compact parameter support. The omitted bulk layer contributes at most its shrinking volume times a uniform bound on F_j and the derivative of psi. Consequently the sum of the trimmed derivative integrals converges to -integral F_j partial_i psi - integral_S n_i[F_j]psi. Define B_ij by this limit. It equals partial_i T_Fj minus n_i[F_j]delta_S, so is a distribution of order at most one; this intrinsic expression proves independence of graph covers and partitions. It agrees with the classical derivative on tests away from S. If the piecewise derivative is L1loc, [[thm-dominated-convergence]] with its absolute value on the compact test support identifies the truncated limit with its ordinary integral. A C1 extension of field and derivatives gives bounded derivatives on each compact closed half-chart and hence this L1 condition. Taking the trace or antisymmetric sum proves divergence and curl with exactly the stated normal sign. For a continuous-value trace without derivative integrability, retain the canonical distributional bulk: for example z sin(z^-2) above z=0, extended by zero below, has continuous trace zero but its classical normal derivative is not locally absolutely integrable. No invalid regular-bulk conclusion is imposed on that branch.

before.title: Inertial charts are related by proper orthochronous affine Lorentz maps, and every such map is a chart transition
before.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space and let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3), (o';e'_0,e'_1,e'_2,e'_3) be two inertial frames with charts x, x' (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Let M be the change-of-basis matrix defined by e'_a = sum_b M^b_a e_b. Then: (i) M is the matrix, in the ordered basis (e_0,...,e_3), of a linear Lorentz map L: V -> V, i.e. L(e_a) = e'_a for all a; M is proper and orthochronous: M^T eta_0 M = eta_0, det M = +1, and M maps the future cone onto the future cone. The same holds for M^{-1} = the matrix of L^{-1}. (ii) The chart transition x' o x^{-1}: R^4 -> R^4 is the affine map u |-> M^{-1}(u - x(o')), whose linear part M^{-1} is a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix; consequently it preserves the quadratic form q(u) := eta_0(u,u) = -(u^0)^2 + |u_vec|^2 of coordinate differences, and it maps future causal coordinate vectors to future causal coordinate vectors. (iii) Conversely, for every proper orthochronous linear Lorentz map L: V -> V and every point c in A, the tuple (c; L e_0, L e_1, L e_2, L e_3) is an inertial frame, and for its chart x_L one has x_L(p) = L^{-1}(x(p) - x(c)) for all p in A. Hence the transitions from the chart x are exactly the affine maps u |-> L^{-1}(u - x(c)) with L ranging over the proper orthochronous linear Lorentz maps and c over A, and the linear parts of transitions are exactly the proper orthochronous Lorentz matrices and their inverses.
before.strategy: Proof plan. (i) Since both ordered bases are eta-orthonormal and positively oriented with future first vector, the linear map L with L(e_a) = e'_a satisfies eta(L e_a, L e_b) = eta(e'_a,e'_b) = eta_ab, so L is a Lorentz map by def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group(a) and its matrix is M; det M = +1 because both bases represent the same orientation, and L(C^+) = C^+ because L e_0 = e'_0 lies in C^+ and a Lorentz map permutes the two components (lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(iv)); alternatively both facts follow from the component structure. The inverse is a Lorentz map of the same type by lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(ii). (ii) The formula x'(p) = M^{-1}(x(p) - x(o')) is exactly the transition identity recorded in def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart; it is affine with linear part M^{-1}, which is proper orthochronous by (i). Preservation of q and of the future cone is then the coordinate form of lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(iii),(iv) applied to L^{-1} (in coordinates, eta_0(M^{-1}u, M^{-1}u) = eta_0(u,u)). (iii) If L is a proper orthochronous linear Lorentz map, then the images L e_a again form an eta-orthonormal basis (eta(L e_a, L e_b) = eta_ab), with future first vector L e_0 (orthochrony) and positive orientation (det L = +1), so (c; L e_0, L e_1, L e_2, L e_3) is an inertial frame. Its linear isomorphism E_L is E o L, hence its chart is x_L(p) = E_L^{-1}(p - c) = L^{-1}(E^{-1}(p - c)) = L^{-1}(x(p) - x(c)). The final statement combines (ii) and (iii); no classification theorem beyond the definitions is used.

Its frame isomorphism is E_L=L o E: R^4 -> V, so E_L^{-1}=E^{-1} o L^{-1}: V -> R^4. With M_L=E^{-1} o L o E, x_L(p)=E^{-1}L^{-1}(p-c)=M_L^{-1}E^{-1}(p-c)=M_L^{-1}(x(p)-x(c)). The coordinate column is acted on by M_L^{-1}, not by the abstract map L^{-1}: V -> V. The final statement combines (ii) and (iii); no classification theorem beyond the definitions is used.

before.title: C^k tensor fields on affine Minkowski space and their inertial components
before.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space, regarded as the smooth 4-manifold with its inertial atlas (lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas), and let Omega be a nonempty open subset of A. Let r,s >= 0 be integers and let k be a nonnegative integer or k = infinity. Write T^{r,s}(V) for the real vector space of type-(r,s) tensors on V, i.e. of multilinear maps (V*)^r x V^s -> R (def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space, def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional), with the identification T_pA = V for every p in A (lem-tangent-space-of-affine-minkowski-space-is-v). A C^k type-(r,s) tensor field on Omega is a map T that assigns to each p in Omega a tensor T(p) in T^{r,s}(V) such that the map Omega -> T^{r,s}(V), p |-> T(p), is of class C^k as a map from the smooth manifold Omega into the finite-dimensional real vector space T^{r,s}(V) (with any norm; finite-dimensional real vector spaces are Banach spaces and all norms are equivalent). The components of T in the inertial chart x of a frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) are the functions T^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s}(p) := T(p)(e*^{a_1},...,e*^{a_r}, e_{b_1},...,e_{b_s}), where (e*^a) is the basis of V* dual to (e_a). Then T is C^k if and only if all its components in one (equivalently, every) inertial chart are C^k functions of x(p), because the identification above is linear; this equivalence is the elementary form of the component law proved in thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation. A type-(0,0) field is called a scalar field, a type-(1,0) field a vector field, and a type-(0,1) field a covector field.
before.strategy: A definition item. Its well-definedness rests on three supplied facts: the tangent spaces of the affine model are canonically identified with V (lem-tangent-space-of-affine-minkowski-space-is-v); the inertial charts form a smooth atlas, so 'C^k as a map on Omega' has a definite meaning (lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas, def-smooth-manifold, def-c-k-map-between-banach-spaces); and T^{r,s}(V) is a finite-dimensional real vector space carrying a canonical smooth structure, so the regularity of p |-> T(p) is a property of the map, not of a chosen chart. The component formula uses the dual basis of the frame's basis of V and the identification T_pA = V; the definition must state explicitly that components are frame-dependent arrays while T(p) is a frame-independent multilinear map, and that the component functions of a C^k field in an inertial chart are C^k (the converse direction is the component law). The equivalence asserted in the statement is proved through the constant linear transition matrices between two frames and their inverses, which are C^infinity; no derivative of the tensor field itself is used in this definition.

before.title: Counterexample: improper and non-orthochronous Lorentz maps, and det = 1 without orthochrony
before.statement: Statement refuted: 'every Lorentz map is proper and orthochronous' and, equivalently, 'every Lorentz map with det L = 1 is orthochronous'. Counterexample: in an inertial frame with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) define the parity map Pi and the time-reversal map T by their matrices Pi = diag(1,-1,-1,-1) and T = diag(-1,1,1,1). Both satisfy M^T eta_0 M = eta_0 because both are diagonal with entries +-1, so both are Lorentz maps; det Pi = -1 and det T = -1, so neither is proper; Pi fixes the time coordinate and hence maps the future cone onto itself, so Pi is orthochronous but improper, while T maps every future timelike vector to a past timelike vector, so T is non-orthochronous. The product Pi T = -I_4 has det = +1 but maps the future cone onto the past cone, so det = 1 does not imply orthochrony. Consequently O(V,eta) strictly contains SO^+(V,eta), the four sign classes of Lorentz maps are genuinely distinct, and the convention of def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group(e), which reserves 'Lorentz transformation' for the proper orthochronous maps, is not automatic.
before.strategy: Every claim is a finite matrix evaluation: the metric condition for diagonal matrices, the determinants, and the action on the time coordinate. The action on the cone is decided by the sign of the transformed time coordinate of a future timelike vector, using the coordinate description of the future cone in lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components. The product Pi T = -I_4 witnesses the second refuted statement. This example is the reason thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra(iv) states explicitly that det = 1 alone does not force orthochrony.

before.title: The reversed triangle inequality and convexity of the future timelike cone
before.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space. (a) Sum of two future timelike vectors. If v,w in V are future timelike then v + w is future timelike and sqrt(-eta(v+w,v+w)) >= sqrt(-eta(v,v)) + sqrt(-eta(w,w)), with equality if and only if v and w are positive proportional. (b) Convexity and concavity along segments. If v,w are future timelike then t v + (1-t) w is future timelike for every real t in [0,1], so the future timelike set is convex; moreover sqrt(-eta(t v + (1-t) w, t v + (1-t) w)) >= t sqrt(-eta(v,v)) + (1-t) sqrt(-eta(w,w)) for every t in [0,1], with equality for 0 < t < 1 if and only if v and w are positive proportional. (c) Finite sums. If v_1,...,v_k are future timelike then v_1 + ... + v_k is future timelike and sqrt(-eta(sum_i v_i, sum_i v_i)) >= sum_i sqrt(-eta(v_i,v_i)), with equality if and only if all v_i are positive multiples of one single future timelike vector. The inequalities are those of the model's eta and are independent of any chart; they are the reversed (Lorentzian) forms of the triangle inequality of the spatial Euclidean structure.
before.strategy: Proof from lem-sr-reverse-cauchy-schwarz-for-future-timelike-vectors and the coordinate description of the cone. (a) Future direction and timelikeness: in an inertial frame write v = (v^0,v_s), w = (w^0,w_s); the coordinate description of the future cone (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components) gives v^0 > |v_s| and w^0 > |w_s|, so (v+w)^0 = v^0 + w^0 > |v_s| + |w_s| >= |v_s + w_s| by the triangle inequality for the Euclidean norm (cor-triangle-inequality-for-inner-product-norm), which is exactly the coordinate description of future timelikeness for v + w. Inequality: sqrt(-eta(v+w,v+w))^2 = -eta(v,v) - 2 eta(v,w) - eta(w,w) = a^2 + b^2 + 2(-eta(v,w)) with a := sqrt(-eta(v,v)), b := sqrt(-eta(w,w)); by the reverse Cauchy-Schwarz inequality -eta(v,w) >= ab, so the square is at least (a+b)^2, and monotonicity of squaring on the nonnegatives (lem-of-square-monotone, thm-of-square-roots) gives the claim. Equality requires -eta(v,w) = ab, which by clause (ii) of the reverse Cauchy-Schwarz lemma is exactly positive proportionality. (b) For 0 <= t <= 1 the vector t v is future timelike when t > 0 (its coordinates are (t v^0, t v_s) with t v^0 > t|v_s| = |t v_s|) and 0 when t = 0; applying (a) to the two future timelike vectors t v and (1-t) w (with the zero vector case handled directly) gives both the membership and the inequality, and the equality statement reduces to the equality case of (a) applied to those two vectors, which are positive proportional exactly when v and w are. (c) Induction on k using (a): thm-induction-principle; the equality case is the conjunction of the equality conditions at each step, which forces all vectors onto one positive ray. All arguments are finite-dimensional and no choice principle is used.

before.title: Total proper time of a piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline
before.statement: Let c>0 be the conversion constant of def-sr-proper-time and let x:[a,b]->A, a<b, be a piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline in the weak sense of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline: x is C^1 on each open piece of a finite partition a=s_0<...<s_m=b, its interior tangents and finite one-sided difference-quotient endpoint tangents are future timelike, and continuous extension of the derivative is not assumed. (i) On each open piece let g_i(t)=sqrt(-eta(x'(t),x'(t)))>0. Define its two-ended improper Riemann integral by the convention of lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability. That lemma proves each value finite and nonnegative; it is positive since g_i is positive and continuous on a compact interior subinterval. (ii) Define total proper time by Delta tau_[a,b](x)=c^{-1} sum_i integral_(s_(i-1),s_i) g_i. The finite sum is independent of the partition, by subdivision additivity and a common refinement. It is independent of the inertial chart because eta and the tangent are chart independent; constant Lorentz changes preserve the density already on each proper truncation. (iii) Define the based proper-time function tau_x(s)=Delta tau_[s0,s](x) for s>=s0, and tau_x(s)=-Delta tau_[s,s0](x) for s<s0, with tau_x(s0)=0, using restrictions and oriented limits. It is strictly increasing, and changing s0 changes only an additive constant. (iv) Corner hypothesis (H) is the special case in which each open-piece derivative has finite limits at both ends and thus extends continuously to the closed piece. Those limits equal the one-sided quotient derivatives. Under (H), each g_i extends continuously and positively to the closed piece, its improper integral equals its ordinary Riemann integral there, and the same finite-sum formula applies. In particular if x is globally C^1 on [a,b], Delta tau(x)=tau(b)-tau(a) of def-sr-proper-time. (v) Delta tau(x)>0. If on piece i the tangent is a constant future timelike vector d_i, the contribution is c^{-1}(s_i-s_(i-1))sqrt(-eta(d_i,d_i)); this gives the finite sum of straight-segment proper times. (vi) Additivity over concatenation: for a<b<d, restrictions of a weak piecewise worldline x on [a,d] satisfy Delta tau_[a,d](x)=Delta tau_[a,b](x)+Delta tau_[b,d](x). Insert b in the partition and use (ii). The definition supplies metric time only; identification with an ideal clock reading is the separate physical clock postulate. No global C^1 inverse, tangent at a kink, or four-acceleration at a kink is asserted.
before.strategy: Well-definedness is lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability: endpoint continuity, finite improper integrals dominated in an inertial chart by the nonnegative time derivative, truncated FTC and partition independence. Strict positivity follows by a compact interior neighborhood on which g_i is positive and continuous. Refinements split each integral, and a common refinement gives independence of the finite partition. Restriction/additivity also give the based function, strict increase and base-point constants. Under (H), if the extended derivative is f_i, truncated FTC gives x(v)-x(u)=integral_u^v f_i. Passing u to the endpoint shows that the one-sided difference quotient is the average of f_i over a shrinking interval and therefore tends to its continuous endpoint value; thus the extension equals the finite quotient tangent. The extended density is continuous and strictly positive on the compact closed piece. Its bounded omitted endpoint tails tend to zero, so its improper value equals the ordinary Riemann value. Global C1 is the one-piece (H) case and agrees with def-sr-proper-time. Constant tangents give the displayed straight-segment calculation directly. All steps are finite-dimensional one-variable real analysis and use no choice principle; no physical premise supplies mathematical integrability.

(vi) Additivity over concatenation: for a<b<d, restrictions of a weak piecewise worldline x on [a,d] satisfy Delta tau_[a,d](x)=Delta tau_[a,b](x)+Delta tau_[b,d](x). Insert b in the partition and use (ii). The definition supplies metric time only; identification with an ideal clock reading is the separate physical clock postulate. No global C^1 inverse, tangent at a kink, or four-acceleration at a kink is asserted.
after.strategy: Well-definedness is lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability: endpoint continuity, finite improper integrals dominated in an inertial chart by the nonnegative time derivative, truncated FTC and partition independence. Strict positivity follows by a compact interior neighborhood on which g_i is positive and continuous. Refinements split each integral, and a common refinement gives independence of the finite partition. Restriction/additivity also give the based function, strict increase and base-point constants. Under (H), if the extended derivative is f_i, truncated FTC gives x(v)-x(u)=integral_u^v f_i. Passing u to the endpoint shows that the one-sided difference quotient is the average of f_i over a shrinking interval and therefore tends to its continuous endpoint value; thus the extension equals the finite quotient tangent. The extended density is continuous and strictly positive on the compact closed piece. Its bounded omitted endpoint tails tend to zero, so its improper value equals the ordinary Riemann value. Global C1 is the one-piece (H) case and agrees with def-sr-proper-time. Constant tangents give the displayed straight-segment calculation directly. All steps are finite-dimensional one-variable real analysis and use no choice principle; no physical premise supplies mathematical integrability.

before.title: Counterexample: a future null curve has no proper-time parametrization
before.statement: Statement refuted: 'every regular C^1 curve of the model admits a proper-time parametrization, with strictly increasing proper-time function and normalized timelike four-velocity'. Counterexample: in an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let k := (1,1,0,0), a future null vector with eta(k,k) = -1 + 1 = 0, and let x(s) := p + s k be the corresponding future null straight line. Then x'(s) = k is nonzero and future null for every s, so x is a regular future null curve in the sense of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, but the proper-time integrand is sqrt(-eta(x',x')) = 0 identically: the associated integral is constant, its derivative vanishes, there is no strictly increasing reparametrization by it, and no normalized four-velocity U with eta(U,U) = -c^2 can be attached to the curve, since every tangent vector is null. The coordinate speed of the curve is c (x^0 = c s and x^1 = s give x^1 = c t), so the curve does describe a light ray; it simply has no massive proper-time parametrization.
before.strategy: Direct computation: eta(k,k) = 0 makes the integrand vanish identically, so the proper-time function is constant and cannot be inverted; the tangent vectors are null, so no timelike unit normalization exists. The example is the concrete reason why def-sr-proper-time carries the future timelike hypothesis and why null rays need their own parametrization. All steps are finite evaluations of the diagonal form.

before.title: Counterexample: a past-directed parametrization of a timelike line is not a worldline
before.statement: Statement refuted: 'if a C^1 curve parametrizes a straight timelike line, then it is a future timelike worldline of the model and the proper-time construction gives the clock reading of its history'. Counterexample: in an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let d := (5,3,0,0), a future timelike displacement with -eta(d,d) = 16, and let x(s) := p - s d for s in [0,1]. Then x'(s) = -d is past timelike for every s, so x is not a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline); but the integrand sqrt(-eta(x',x')) = 4 is the same as for the future-parametrized line s |-> p + s d, so the proper-time integral alone does not distinguish the two parametrizations. The model's clock reading attaches to the future-directed history: the same image with the parametrization s |-> p + s d is the worldline, and x is its orientation reversal. This is why the parametrization, and not merely the image of the curve, is part of the definition of a worldline.
before.strategy: Direct evaluation: eta(-d,-d) = eta(d,d) = -16, so the integrand is identical for the two parametrizations; the future/past alternative is decided by the time orientation of the model, not by the sign of eta(x',x'). Every step is a finite computation.

before.title: Adopted Minkowski physical model of the electromagnetic framework
before.statement: Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework: (i) the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of the mathematical model [[def-em-minkowski-affine-space]], together with the conversion constant $c>0$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]], is the spacetime of the framework: its points represent idealized physical events, displacements represent idealized spacetime separations, and the causal classification of the model is the framework's causal structure; (ii) the inertial frames and charts of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] are the inertial descriptions of the framework, and changes of description are the proper orthochronous isometries adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]; (iii) the ideal clock reading rule along future timelike curves and the identification of ideal vacuum light rays with future null straight lines, both with the same constant $c$, are those adopted in [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]; (iv) the laboratory description of fields and sources is the restricted inertial chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the spatial Euclidean structure and the SI conventions of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Status and scope: the mathematical model defines the geometry and its theorems prove geometric facts only; that physical events are described by the model, that ideal clocks read the stated proper time and that ideal vacuum light follows null straight lines are adopted assumptions, not deductions from experiment or from the mathematical axioms. The special-relativity postulates adopted here do not by themselves select the Maxwell equations, a force law or any matter model: the electromagnetic equations and couplings of this framework are further postulates of it. The framework is classical, flat and non-quantum; gravitational curvature, quantum fields and measurement postulates are outside its scope.
before.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it records the adopted physical reading of the mathematical Minkowski model of [[def-em-minkowski-affine-space]] and reuses the two special-relativity physical postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] with the shared constant $c$ as the vacuum propagation constant. The exposition must separate what the mathematical model fixes (the affine geometry, its causal cones, its frames) from what is adopted (the event interpretation, the clock and light interpretation, the inertial-description equivalence). It must also state that Maxwell's equations and the Lorentz coupling are additional postulates not implied by the SR assumptions, and it asserts no empirical measurement or verification.

The cone notation is bridged explicitly: the $C^+$ of [[def-em-minkowski-affine-space]] consists of all nonzero future causal vectors; the $C^+$ in the SR affine model is the open future timelike component. before.title: Collinear boost composition and the relativistic velocity-addition law
before.statement: Let B(beta_1 e) and B(beta_2 e) be passive boosts in a common spatial direction e, where e is a unit vector of the frame's spatial three-space and beta_1, beta_2 in (-1,1) are real parameters (def-lorentz-boost, def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame). Then B(beta_1 e) B(beta_2 e) = B(beta e) with beta := (beta_1 + beta_2)/(1 + beta_1 beta_2), and |beta| < 1; in particular the two collinear boosts commute, B(beta_1 e)B(beta_2 e) = B(beta_2 e)B(beta_1 e), and B(beta_1 e) B(-beta_2 e) = B(((beta_1 - beta_2)/(1 - beta_1 beta_2)) e). The parameter is accordingly additive under composition (velocity addition in units of the conversion constant: if beta_i are the dimensionless parameters, the composed parameter is the displayed beta and not beta_1 + beta_2), and no composition of two boosts in a common direction ever leaves the open interval (-1,1).
before.strategy: Compute the product of the two matrices on the common (e_0,e)-plane: both boosts act as the identity on the common perpendicular P^perp and fix no other direction, so the product is again the identity on P^perp and the 2x2 matrix product [[gamma_1,-gamma_1 beta_1],[-gamma_1 beta_1,gamma_1]] [[gamma_2,-gamma_2 beta_2],[-gamma_2 beta_2,gamma_2]] equals gamma_1 gamma_2 (1 + beta_1 beta_2) [[1, -(beta_1+beta_2)/(1+beta_1 beta_2)], [-(beta_1+beta_2)/(1+beta_1 beta_2), 1]], which is the boost matrix with parameter beta given above and gamma = gamma_1 gamma_2 (1 + beta_1 beta_2). The algebra proving the display uses gamma_i^2 (1 - beta_i^2) = 1 and the rational power laws. To see |beta| < 1: the denominator 1 + beta_1 beta_2 > 0 because |beta_1 beta_2| < 1, and |beta_1 + beta_2| < 1 + beta_1 beta_2 is equivalent to (beta_1 + beta_2)^2 < (1 + beta_1 beta_2)^2, i.e. to (1 - beta_1^2)(1 - beta_2^2) > 0, which holds since |beta_i| < 1. The minus case is the same multiplication with beta_2 replaced by -beta_2 and 1 - beta_1 beta_2 > 0. Since the identity on P^perp and the matrices on P together define the whole map, the computation is complete; no continuity or limiting argument is used.

before.title: Transformation of tensor, covector, derivative and current components under affine Lorentz maps
before.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space, let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is the affine map x'(p) = Lambda x(p) + b with linear part Lambda (a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix by lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz), and let Omega be an open subset of A. Let J: Omega -> V, k, and T be a C^k vector field, a C^k covector field and a C^k type-(r,s) tensor field on Omega in the sense of def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space, with components J^a, k_a and T^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} in the chart x, and primed components in the chart x'. Then: (i) J'^a = Lambda^a_b J^b: a contravariant index gains the factor Lambda^a_b, i.e. components transform by multiplication with the transition matrix. (ii) k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b: a covariant index gains the factor (Lambda^{-1})^b_a. If theta(p) = k_a x^a(p) + theta_0 is an affine scalar function with constant covector k and constant theta_0, then theta(p) = k'_a x'^a(p) + theta'_0 with k' as above and theta'_0 := theta_0 - k'_a b^a, so the phase function is invariant when the constant term is transformed together with the covector. (iii) T'^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} = Lambda^{a_1}_{c_1} ... Lambda^{a_r}_{c_r} (Lambda^{-1})^{d_1}_{b_1} ... (Lambda^{-1})^{d_s}_{b_s} T^{c_1...c_r}_{d_1...d_s}: every contravariant index gains a factor Lambda and every covariant index a factor Lambda^{-1}, and the law is consistent with the multilinear evaluation of T(p) after substituting the transformed basis. Every contraction of one contravariant with one covariant index is invariant, and the metric components satisfy eta'_{ab} = eta_{ab}. (iv) The coordinate partial derivatives satisfy partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b wherever the derivatives exist. Consequently the divergence of a vector field is invariant, partial'_a J'^a = partial_a J^a, and for a C^1 type-(2,0) field T one has partial'_a T'^{ab} = Lambda^b_c partial_a T^{ac}. (v) Alternating covariant tensor fields transform by the covariant law on each slot; the oriented volume form of the model satisfies epsilon'_{abcd} = epsilon_{abcd}, since det Lambda = +1, whereas a general Lorentz matrix with det = -1 changes its sign. (vi) Let J be a C^1 vector field with components (J^0,J^1,J^2,J^3) in an inertial chart, and write the spatial block as J_cov := (J^1,J^2,J^3) and denote by partial_i the spatial partial derivatives in the chart. Then the continuity equation partial_a J^a = 0 is equivalent to partial_0 J^0 + sum_i partial_i J^i = 0, and under the passive boost with parameter beta (Lambda = B(beta), Lambda^{-1} = B(-beta)) the components transform as J'^0 = gamma(J^0 - beta . J_cov), J'_cov = J_cov + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . J_cov) beta - gamma beta J^0. (vii) If U is a C^1 future timelike vector field and rho_0 a C^1 scalar field, then J:=rho_0 U is a C^1 vector field and its first component is J^0=rho_0 U^0. Future timelikeness gives U^0>0 in every inertial chart, so define the normalized chart direction u:=U/U^0 and the coordinate density rho:=J^0. Then u^0=1, u^i=U^i/U^0, rho=rho_0 U^0, and J=rho u pointwise. The coordinate density rho and scalar multiplier rho_0 are different objects: rho=rho_0 if and only if rho_0(U^0−1)=0; at points where rho_0!=0 equality holds exactly when U^0=1. The vector u is a normalized chart direction; it is not assumed to have unit or four-velocity normalization. In an x^0=ct convention the associated spatial coordinate velocity, if interpreted as such, has components c u^i; physical current/density identification requires its own model premise. Interpretation boundary: the identification of a physical charge-current with a vector field, and of rho with a measured charge density, is a model premise of the electromagnetic framework; this item is a statement about the transformation of components of specified fields and does not by itself assert that any physical current transforms as a vector.
before.strategy: Proof plan. (i) and (ii) are the definitions of components: for a vector field, J'(p) = sum_a J'^a(p) partial'_a|_p and partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b, so comparing coefficients with J = sum_b J^b partial_b gives J'^a = Lambda^a_b J^b; the covector transform is the dual statement k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b. The affine phase invariance in (ii) is the displayed substitution k_a x^a = k'_c x'^c - k'_c b^c. (iii) is the multilinear evaluation: writing T(p) on the transformed basis and using the definition of the components, each contravariant slot contributes Lambda and each covariant slot the inverse; the contraction claim follows from (Lambda^{-1})^a_b Lambda^b_c = delta^a_c, and eta'_{ab} = eta_{ab} is the matrix form of the defining Lorentz property of Lambda. (iv) is the chain rule for the transition x' = Lambda x + b: partial'_a = (partial x^c / partial x'^a) partial_c = (Lambda^{-1})^c_a partial_c; substituting into partial'_a J'^a and using (i) gives the invariance of the divergence, and the (2,0) case follows by the same substitution with the two contravariant factors. after.title: Transformation of tensor, covector, derivative and current components under affine Lorentz maps
after.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space, let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is the affine map x'(p) = Lambda x(p) + b with linear part Lambda (a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix by lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz), and let Omega be an open subset of A. Let ell be a nonnegative integer or infinity as in def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space. Let J: Omega -> V, k, and T be a C^ell vector field, a C^ell covector field and a C^ell type-(r,s) tensor field on Omega in the sense of def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space, with components J^a, k_a and T^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} in the chart x, and primed components in the chart x'. Then: (i) J'^a = Lambda^a_b J^b: a contravariant index gains the factor Lambda^a_b, i.e. components transform by multiplication with the transition matrix. (ii) k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b: a covariant index gains the factor (Lambda^{-1})^b_a. If theta(p) = k_a x^a(p) + theta_0 is an affine scalar function with constant covector k and constant theta_0, then theta(p) = k'_a x'^a(p) + theta'_0 with k' as above and theta'_0 := theta_0 - k'_a b^a, so the phase function is invariant when the constant term is transformed together with the covector. (iii) T'^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} = Lambda^{a_1}_{c_1} ... Lambda^{a_r}_{c_r} (Lambda^{-1})^{d_1}_{b_1} ... (Lambda^{-1})^{d_s}_{b_s} T^{c_1...c_r}_{d_1...d_s}: every contravariant index gains a factor Lambda and every covariant index a factor Lambda^{-1}, and the law is consistent with the multilinear evaluation of T(p) after substituting the transformed basis. Every contraction of one contravariant with one covariant index is invariant, and the metric components satisfy eta'_{ab} = eta_{ab}. (vi) Let J be a C^1 vector field with components (J^0,J^1,J^2,J^3) in an inertial chart, and write the spatial block as J_cov := (J^1,J^2,J^3) and denote by partial_i the spatial partial derivatives in the chart. Then the continuity equation partial_a J^a = 0 is equivalent to partial_0 J^0 + sum_i partial_i J^i = 0, and under the passive boost with |beta|<1 (Lambda = B(beta), Lambda^{-1} = B(-beta)), the beta=0 branch is the identity J'=J. For beta!=0 the components transform as J'^0 = gamma(J^0 - beta . J_cov), J'_cov = J_cov + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . J_cov) beta - gamma beta J^0. The vector u is a normalized chart direction; it is not assumed to have unit or four-velocity normalization. before.title: The operational radar protocol of an ideal observer
before.statement: Adopt the ideal-clock and ideal-light assumptions of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and the SI conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Let x: I -> A be a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline) with proper-time function tau (def-sr-proper-time), and let s_- < s_+ be parameter values. Suppose an event q and the events e_- := x(s_-), e_+ := x(s_+) satisfy: q - e_- is future null and e_+ - q is future null (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). Under the adopted ideal-light assumption an ideal ray is emitted at e_-, reaches q, and an ideal ray emitted at q reaches e_+; the event q is idealized as an instantaneous reflection that changes nothing else. The radar protocol of the observer assigns to q (i) the radar time tau_rad(q) := (tau(s_-)+tau(s_+))/2, the ideal clock's reading midway between emission and reception, and (ii) the radar distance rho_rad(q) := c(tau(s_+)-tau(s_-))/2, half the round-trip light time multiplied by c. Two events measured by the same observer are radar-simultaneous when their radar times agree. The assignment does not change under increasing reparametrizations of the observer's worldline, because tau does not (lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance). Conventions and scope: (a) the protocol is a definition of an operational assignment conditional on the existence of the emission, reflection and reception events, and it assumes an available ideal reflector and ideal apparatus; (b) the split of the round trip into a 'time' and a 'distance' uses the symmetric convention in which half of the round-trip time is assigned to the outgoing and half to the returning segment; the protocol determines the round-trip quantity tau(s_+)-tau(s_-) operationally, while the derived one-way assignment is a convention and does not measure a one-way light speed independently of a synchronization convention; (c) nothing is claimed about accelerated observers, dispersive or absorbing media, finite-resolution apparatus, global single-valuedness or detector models, and no measurement outcome, statistical inference or empirical comparison is asserted.
before.strategy: Definition item with formulation obligations. (i) The assigned quantities are defined from the proper-time function and the events; the stated existence hypotheses make them well defined, and invariance under increasing reparametrization is lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance. (ii) The two null segments are the operational content of the adopted ideal-light assumption (post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light); the reflection is an idealization, so the definition does not describe a physical mirror. (iii) The symmetric half-split is stated as a convention, not derived; its consequences for inertial observers are proved in pthm-sr-radar-synchronization-of-inertial-observers below, and the failure of global ring synchronization for rotating observers is exhibited by the explicit example on this page. (iv) No proof is manufactured: the item introduces an operational assignment, and its only mathematical content is well-definedness. The scope clause carries the idealizations of the postulates to every consumer.
before.physical_scope: Ideal radar measurement by a single observer with an ideal clock and ideal vacuum light rays modeled as future null straight lines, in flat classical special-relativistic spacetime; defines round-trip radar time and radar distance under a stated symmetric convention. Excludes real apparatus and finite resolution, dispersive or absorbing media, reflector and detector models, accelerated-observer global synchronization claims, one-way light-speed measurements, and every empirical or statistical claim; the idealizations of the adopted postulates travel to all consumers.

before.title: Existence of an inertial frame whose time axis is a prescribed future timelike direction
before.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space, let d in V be a future timelike displacement and put T := sqrt(-eta(d,d)) > 0 and n := d/T. Then: (i) eta(n,n) = -1 and n is future timelike, so n is a future unit timelike vector; (ii) for every event o there is an inertial frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) of the model with e_0 = n; (iii) for the inertial chart x of any such frame one has x(o + lambda d) = (lambda T, 0, 0, 0) for every real lambda; in particular x(o) = 0 and x(o + d) = (T, 0, 0, 0). Consequently, for any two events p,q with q - p = d, the chart of such a frame represents the displacement q - p by the coordinate vector (T,0,0,0): the spatial coordinates of p and q agree and their time coordinates differ by T.
before.strategy: Proof. (i) Bilinearity gives eta(n,n) = eta(d,d)/T^2 = -1 (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia, def-rational-power), and n is future timelike because the future timelike set is closed under multiplication by the positive real 1/T (cor-sr-reverse-triangle-and-future-cone-convexity, clause (b)). (ii) Fix any inertial frame with origin o, with basis (f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3) (lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist). Let (n^0, n_s) be the coordinates of n in this frame. Since n is future timelike, the coordinate description of the future cone (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components) gives n^0 > |n_s| >= 0, and eta(n,n) = -(n^0)^2 + |n_s|^2 = -1 gives (n^0)^2 = 1 + |n_s|^2 > 0, so the boost parameter beta := n_s/n^0 (a vector of R^3) satisfies |beta| = |n_s|/n^0 < 1 (def-lorentz-boost). Let B := B(beta) be the passive boost of the frame. By lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse (iv), B n = f_0; by the same lemma (i) and (iii), B is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map with inverse B^{-1} = B(-beta). Define the ordered basis e_0 := n and e_i := B^{-1} f_i for i = 1,2,3; then it is the image under the Lorentz map B^{-1} of the eta-orthonormal basis (f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3) with B^{-1} f_0 = n = e_0, so it is eta-orthonormal with eta(e_0,e_0) = -1 and eta(e_0,e_i) = 0 (lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure (i),(iii)); its first vector is future, and it is positively oriented because B^{-1} is proper, hence preserves the oriented volume form and the orientation class (lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure (iii)). Therefore (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) is an inertial frame with first vector n (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). (iii) For its chart x(p) = E^{-1}(p - o) with E(u) = sum_a u^a e_a one has E(1,0,0,0) = e_0 = n, hence x(o + lambda d) = E^{-1}(lambda d) = lambda T E^{-1}(n) = lambda T (1,0,0,0), and x(o) = 0. No choice principle is used: the construction uses one finite-dimensional basis and the explicit boost of def-lorentz-boost.

before.title: Counterexample: noncollinear boosts do not commute
before.statement: Statement refuted: 'for all beta_1, beta_2 in R^3 with |beta_i| < 1 the passive boosts satisfy B(beta_1)B(beta_2) = B(beta_2)B(beta_1)'. Counterexample: take beta_1 = (3/5,0,0) and beta_2 = (0,3/5,0), with gamma = 5/4. Then B(beta_1)B(beta_2) = [[25/16, -3/4, -15/16, 0],[-15/16, 5/4, 9/16, 0],[-3/4, 0, 5/4, 0],[0,0,0,1]], B(beta_2)B(beta_1) = [[25/16, -15/16, -3/4, 0],[-3/4, 5/4, 0, 0],[-15/16, 9/16, 5/4, 0],[0,0,0,1]]. The two matrices differ, for instance in the (0,1) entry (-3/4 versus -15/16), the (0,2) entry (-15/16 versus -3/4) and the (2,1) entry (0 versus 9/16). Hence the composition of boosts is order dependent; the counterexample does not claim that the two compositions fail to be Lorentz maps (both are proper orthochronous Lorentz maps, as products of such), only that the group is not abelian and that the boost composition law is a collinear law.
before.strategy: The two products are computed directly from the 4x4 boost matrices with beta = 3/5 (the same matrices used in ex-sr-one-plus-one-boost-matrix, extended by identities off their planes), and a single differing entry refutes the asserted commutation. The source's Section 8.3.2 reports the same phenomenon numerically for boosts along x and y; here the exact rational matrices are displayed and the (2,1) entry 9/16 versus 0 witnesses the difference. The counterexample is consistent with lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition, which asserts commutation only for boosts in a common direction, and with lem-boost-rotation-factorization, which explains the discrepancy as a spatial rotation.

before.title: Norms of four-velocity and four-acceleration, and the observer rest-space decomposition
before.statement: Let c > 0 and let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space. (a) Norm of the four-velocity. Let x: I -> A be a C^1 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration). Then eta(U(s),U(s)) = -c^2 for every s in I; equivalently the dimensionless four-velocity u = U/c satisfies eta(u,u) = -1, and U(s) is future timelike. Thus the four-velocity of a worldline lies on the future unit hyperboloid. (b) Orthogonality of the four-acceleration. If x is C^2 at s, then eta(U(s),A(s)) = 0: the four-acceleration has no component along the four-velocity; if in addition A(s) is nonzero, then A(s) is spacelike. (c) Rest space and projection. Let n in V be future unit timelike, eta(n,n) = -1, and put n^perp := {v in V : eta(n,v) = 0}. Then n^perp is a 3-dimensional linear subspace of V, the restriction of eta to n^perp is positive definite, and the map h: V -> V, h(v) := v + eta(n,v) n, is linear, idempotent with h o h = h, has image n^perp and kernel span(n), satisfies h(n) = 0 and eta(n,h(v)) = 0 for all v in V, and every v in V has the unique decomposition v = -eta(n,v) n + h(v). Moreover |w| := sqrt(eta(w,w)) defines a norm on n^perp. (d) Relative velocity and Lorentz factor. Let n and u be future unit timelike vectors, put gamma := -eta(n,u) and w := c h(u)/gamma. Then gamma >= 1, w lies in n^perp, u = gamma (n + w/c), |w|^2 = c^2 (1 - gamma^{-2}) < c^2, gamma = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and gamma = 1 if and only if u = n. The vector w is the velocity of a worldline with four-velocity c u relative to the observer n and gamma is its Lorentz factor. (e) Coordinate form. Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame and let y be a C^1 future timelike worldline whose inertial coordinates are t |-> (c t, r(t)), with coordinate velocity w(t) := r'(t) in R^3 and, when y is C^2, coordinate acceleration a(t) := w'(t). Then |w(t)| < c, the four-velocity is U = gamma_w (c,w) with gamma_w := (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and the four-acceleration is A = gamma_w (d/dt)(gamma_w (c,w)), so that A^0 = gamma_w^4 (w.a)/c and A_vec = gamma_w^2 a + gamma_w^4 (w.a) w/c^2; consequently eta(A,A) = gamma_w^4 |a|^2 + gamma_w^6 (w.a)^2/c^2 >= 0, with eta(A,A) = 0 if and only if a = 0, and eta(U,A) = 0. For the observer n = e_0 of the chart, clauses (c) and (d) specialize to gamma = gamma_w and w_rel = w. (f) Scope. The statement is a theorem about the affine Minkowski model with a fixed positive constant c; it asserts no clock reading and identifies no physical four-velocity. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Proof in dependency order; the hard part is (c), which is pure algebra plus one coordinate computation, and the remaining clauses follow from it. (c) Fix an eta-orthonormal basis with e_0 timelike (lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis; use an inertial frame of def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Write n = n^0 e_0 + n_s and v = v^0 e_0 + v_s with n_s,v_s in S = span(e_1,e_2,e_3), where eta restricts to the positive definite delta with norm |.| (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame). From eta(n,n) = -(n^0)^2 + |n_s|^2 = -1 one gets (n^0)^2 = 1 + |n_s|^2 > 0. For v with eta(n,v) = -n^0 v^0 + delta(n_s,v_s) = 0 one has v^0 = delta(n_s,v_s)/n^0, hence eta(v,v) = -(v^0)^2 + |v_s|^2 = |v_s|^2 - delta(n_s,v_s)^2/(n^0)^2 >= |v_s|^2 (1 - |n_s|^2/(n^0)^2) = |v_s|^2/(n^0)^2 >= 0 by the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for delta (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite); equality forces |v_s| = 0 and then v^0 = 0, so v = 0 and the restriction is positive definite. The map v_s |-> v^0 e_0 + v_s with v^0 = delta(n_s,v_s)/n^0 is a linear bijection S -> n^perp, so n^perp is 3-dimensional. The properties of h are immediate from bilinearity of eta (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia, def-linear-map): eta(n,h(v)) = eta(n,v) + eta(n,v)eta(n,n) = 0, so h(v) lies in n^perp; h(n) = n + eta(n,n)n = 0; h(h(v)) = h(v) + eta(n,h(v))n = h(v); and v = -eta(n,v)n + h(v) is unique because the two summands lie in span(n) and n^perp, which meet only in 0. (a) By def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, U = x'/tau' with tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(x',x')), so eta(U,U) = eta(x',x')/(tau')^2 = eta(x',x') c^2/(-eta(x',x')) = -c^2; timelikeness and the future direction of U follow from those of x' and positivity of 1/tau'. (b) eta(U,U) is the constant -c^2 along a C^2 worldline; differentiating componentwise in an eta-orthonormal basis with thm-algebra-of-derivatives gives 0 = (d/ds) eta(U,U) = 2 eta(U,U'), hence eta(U,U') = 0, and dividing by tau' > 0 gives eta(U,A) = 0. If A(s) is nonzero, then A(s) lies in (U(s)/c)^perp, a positive definite space by (c), so eta(A,A) > 0: A(s) is spacelike. (d) By (c), h(u) lies in n^perp and u = gamma n + h(u) with gamma = -eta(n,u). First, gamma > 0: in the inertial frame of (c), future timelikeness of n and u gives n^0 > |n_s| and u^0 > |u_s| (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components), so eta(n,u) = -n^0 u^0 + delta(n_s,u_s) <= -n^0 u^0 + |n_s||u_s| < 0. Second, eta(u,u) = gamma^2 eta(n,n) + eta(h(u),h(u)) = -gamma^2 + |h(u)|^2 = -1, so |h(u)|^2 = gamma^2 - 1 >= 0, giving gamma >= 1; substituting w = c h(u)/gamma gives |w|^2 = c^2 (gamma^2-1)/gamma^2 = c^2(1 - gamma^{-2}) < c^2, and solving for gamma gives gamma = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2} and gamma = 1 iff h(u) = 0 iff u = n. (e) In the chart the coordinate path is t |-> (c t, r(t)), so x' = (c,w) and -eta(x',x') = c^2 - |w|^2 > 0 by future timelikeness, giving |w| < c and tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(c^2-|w|^2) = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{1/2} = 1/gamma_w; hence U = x'/tau' = gamma_w (c,w). For C^2 paths, d gamma_w/dt = gamma_w^3 (w.a)/c^2 by thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives (applied to the power -1/2) with the chain rule, and collecting terms in A = gamma_w dU/dt gives the displayed components; expanding eta(A,A) in the diagonal form and using gamma_w^2(1-|w|^2/c^2) = 1 gives eta(A,A) = gamma_w^4 |a|^2 + gamma_w^6 (w.a)^2/c^2 >= 0 with equality iff |a| = 0, and eta(U,A) = 0 agrees with (b). (f) The specialization n = e_0 is the evaluation h(u) = u - u^0 e_0 = (0, w/c gamma_w) and gamma = u^0 = gamma_w, so w_rel = w. No choice principle is used; all arguments are finite-dimensional or one-variable calculus.

before.title: Proper-time derivative of a vector field along a worldline and the four-force notation
before.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^1$ future timelike worldline with proper-time function $\tau:I\to J$ and inverse $\rho:J\to I$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]).
(a) For a $C^1$ map $P:I\to V$ define its proper-time derivative $\dot P:I\to V$ by
$$\dot P(s):=\frac{P'(s)}{\tau'(s)},$$
where $P'$ is the derivative of $P$ with respect to the worldline parameter, taken componentwise in any affine basis of $V$; the result does not depend on the basis because two affine bases differ by a constant invertible linear map. Equivalently $\dot P(s)=(P\circ\rho)'(\tau(s))$, so $\dot P$ is the derivative of the proper-time parametrised field $P\circ\rho$. Since $\tau'(s)>0$ by [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]], $\dot P$ is well defined and continuous whenever $P$ is $C^1$.
(b) If $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant and $U$ the four-velocity of $x$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), then $F:=\dot P$ is called the four-force on the particle; in an inertial frame $F$ has the components of the derivative of the four-momentum with respect to proper time.
(c) This item introduces a derivative and a name only. It asserts no force law, no field equation, no equation of motion and no existence or uniqueness of solutions; the identities satisfied by $F$ for a stipulated four-momentum field are proved in [[lem-sr-four-force-and-work-energy-identities]], and a physical force law requires a further model premise.
before.strategy: Definition item. Obligations: (i) the division by $\tau'$ is legitimate because $\tau'>0$ ([[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]); (ii) the equivalence $\dot P(s)=(P\circ\rho)'(\tau(s))$ is the chain rule along the reparametrisation, $\rho$ being the inverse of the increasing function $\tau$; (iii) componentwise differentiation in one affine basis and change of basis commute because the transition map is constant and linear, so the definition is basis-free; (iv) no dynamics is imported: $F$ is a derived vector field attached to a given $P$, not a prescribed law. No choice principle is used.

before.title: The proper orthochronous Lorentz group: boosts, rotations, unique factorization and invariants
before.statement: Let (V,eta) be the Lorentz vector space with time orientation C^+ and let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame of the model. Then: (i) For every beta in R^3 with |beta| < 1 the passive boost B(beta) is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map, B(beta)^{-1} = B(-beta), and for collinear boosts B(beta_1 e)B(beta_2 e) = B(((beta_1 + beta_2)/(1 + beta_1 beta_2)) e) for every unit spatial vector e and beta_1, beta_2 in (-1,1); in particular collinear boosts commute. For each fixed unit spatial axis e and scalar b in (-1,1), the collinear boost B(b e) has b = tanh r for a unique scalar rapidity r in R; rapidities add for boosts along that same fixed axis. This signed scalar rapidity statement does not identify a vector beta in R^3 with the scalar tanh r. (ii) SO^+(V,eta) is a subgroup of O(V,eta), which is a subgroup of GL(V); every passive boost B(beta) and every spatial rotation of the frame (extended by fixing e_0) belongs to SO^+(V,eta). (iii) Every L in SO^+(V,eta) has a unique factorization L = B(-beta) Rhat with |beta| < 1 and Rhat the extension of a spatial rotation of the frame; here beta = u_vec/u^0 where (u^0,u_vec) are the coordinates of u = L e_0. Consequently every proper orthochronous Lorentz map is the product of a passive boost and a spatial rotation (in that order), and L is itself a passive boost if and only if the rotation is the identity. (iv) Every L in SO^+(V,eta) preserves the interval eta(v,v), the causal classification of every nonzero vector, the future and past closed cones, the orientation and the oriented volume form of the model: epsilon(Lv_0,...,Lv_3) = epsilon(v_0,...,v_3) for all v_0,...,v_3 in V. An arbitrary element L of O(V,eta) has det L = +-1 and either preserves or interchanges the future and past cones, and det L = 1 alone does not force L(C^+) = C^+.
before.strategy: Assembly of the page's proved lemmas, with each clause assigned to its supplier. (i) is lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse plus lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition plus the fixed-axis scalar bijection r |-> tanh r of lem-rapidity-parametrization-of-collinear-boosts. The vector boost claims use vector beta; only B(b e) with a specified unit axis uses signed scalar b and r. (ii) is lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(ii) for the subgroup statements; boosts lie in SO^+(V,eta) by (i), and a spatial rotation Rhat is a Lorentz map fixing the future timelike vector e_0, hence proper of determinant one and orthochronous by lem-boost-rotation-factorization(iii). (iii) is lem-boost-rotation-factorization(ii),(iv),(v). (iv) combines lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(iii),(iv) with det-preservation; the final sentence records the failure of the converse of 'proper implies orthochronous' and is witnessed by the B-page counterexample cex-sr-discrete-lorentz-maps-are-not-proper-orthochronous, whose claim is the explicit matrix computation, not an input here. The proof contract must restate the hypotheses (frame fixed, |beta| < 1, L proper orthochronous) and cite each lemma as the whole content of its clause; no clause may be asserted without the corresponding cited result.

before.title: Four-velocity norm and four-acceleration orthogonality for the model's clocks
before.statement: Adopt the postulates of the model: post-sr-inertial-covariance and post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light of the spacetime-primitives page together with post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis of this page, and let c and the SI coordinates be those of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Let x: I -> A be the history of an ideal clock of the model, a C^1 future timelike worldline (C^2 where acceleration is used), with proper time tau, four-velocity U = dx/dtau and, when x is C^2, four-acceleration A = dU/dtau (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration). Then: (i) the reading of the ideal clock between parameter values s_1 < s_2 equals tau(s_2) - tau(s_1); (ii) eta(U,U) = -c^2 everywhere, so U is a future unit timelike vector with the unit of a velocity; (iii) if x is C^2 at s, then eta(U(s),A(s)) = 0 and A(s) is zero or spacelike, with unit of acceleration; (iv) if the clock is free (no interaction), then its four-velocity is constant along the worldline and A = 0 identically; (v) for an ideal observer at the same event, described by a future unit timelike vector n = U_o/c with eta(n,n) = -1, the clock's speed relative to the observer is |w| = c sqrt(1 - gamma^{-2}) with gamma = -eta(n, U/c) >= 1, so it is strictly less than c, and gamma = 1 exactly when the clock's four-velocity equals the observer's. Scope and qualification: this is a conditional statement about the adopted model; it asserts no measurement outcome, contains no statistical inference, and inherits the idealizations of the postulates (ideal point particles, ideal clocks, flat spacetime, no gravitational or quantum effects).
before.strategy: Conditional deduction from the adopted premises; the mathematical content is thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition. (i) is the clock hypothesis of post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis together with the proper-time definition, restated for the page's worldline calculus. (ii) and (iii) are clauses (a) and (b) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition, with U identified with the clock's four-velocity by the clock hypothesis; the identification supplies the physical meaning of U, the identities are mathematical. (iv) By the free-trajectory clause there are p and future timelike v with x(s) = p + (s - s_0)v; then x' = v is constant, tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(v,v)) is constant and positive, so U = x'/tau' is the constant vector c v/sqrt(-eta(v,v)), and A = U'/tau' = 0. (v) is clause (d) of the mathematical theorem, with the observer vector n allowed to be any future unit timelike vector; post-sr-inertial-covariance licenses the interpretation of observers and clocks as model objects and def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions fixes c and the units of the speed. The proof must not upgrade the conditional statement to a claim about nature and must carry the idealizations to the conclusion.
