before.title: Fermi-Walker transport along a timelike worldline
before.statement: Let x: I -> A be a C^2 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U = dx/dtau and four-acceleration A = dU/dtau (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration), so eta(U,U) = -c^2 and eta(U,A) = 0 (thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition), and let X: I -> V be a C^1 field along x (def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve). (a) The Fermi-Walker derivative of X is D_FW X/dtau := X' - (1/c^2)(eta(A,X)U - eta(U,X)A), where X' is the ordinary V-valued derivative of X (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (d)). X is Fermi-Walker transported along x when D_FW X/dtau = 0, i.e. when X' = (1/c^2)(eta(A,X)U - eta(U,X)A). (b) The four-velocity is Fermi-Walker transported: D_FW U/dtau = A - (1/c^2)(eta(A,U)U - eta(U,U)A) = A - A = 0, using eta(U,A) = 0 and eta(U,U) = -c^2. (c) If A = 0 on an interval then Fermi-Walker transport coincides there with ordinary (parallel) transport X' = 0; if A is not zero, the definition includes exactly the correction that transports the time leg U/c itself. (d) A Fermi-Walker transported tetrad along x is a tuple (E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3) of C^1 fields along x with E_0 = U/c and every E_a Fermi-Walker transported; existence from a prescribed initial tetrad and preservation of the tetrad conditions are proved in the following lemma. The physical interpretation (a nonrotating spatial frame carried by an accelerated observer) is not asserted here; only the transport rule is defined.
before.strategy: Definition item. (i) The transport equation is a first-order linear differential equation for a V-valued field along x with coefficients determined by U and A, continuous when x is C^2; the ordinary derivative X' is the covariant derivative because T_pA is canonically identified with V (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (d)). (ii) The identity in (b) is a short computation using eta(U,U) = -c^2 and eta(U,A) = 0 from thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition. (iii) The contrast with parallel transport in (c) is immediate from the definition, and (d) fixes terminology. (iv) Existence, uniqueness and preservation properties are deliberately not claimed here; they are supplied by lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness and thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples. No choice principle is used.

before.title: Simultaneity slices and rest distance relative to a future unit timelike vector
before.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space and let n be a future unit timelike vector, eta(n,n) = -1. (a) Rest space. The rest space of n is the hyperplane n^perp = {v in V : eta(n,v) = 0}; by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (c) it is a three-dimensional linear subspace on which eta restricts to a positive-definite symmetric form, and the orthogonal projection onto it is h(v) = v + eta(n,v)n. (b) Simultaneity slice. For p in A the simultaneity slice of p relative to n is the affine hyperplane H(p,n) := p + n^perp = {q in A : eta(n,q-p) = 0}; it contains p and is three-dimensional, not a single point. (c) Simultaneity relation. Define q ~_n q' iff eta(n,q'-q) = 0, i.e. iff q'-q lies in n^perp. Then ~_n is an equivalence relation on A whose equivalence classes are exactly the slices H(p,n); reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity are consequences of n^perp being a linear subspace and not physical assumptions. (d) Rest distance. For p,q with q in H(p,n) define d_n(p,q) := sqrt(eta(q-p,q-p)). after.title: Simultaneity slices and rest distance relative to a future unit timelike vector
after.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space and let n be a future unit timelike vector, eta(n,n) = -1. (a) Rest space. (b) Simultaneity slice. For p in A the simultaneity slice of p relative to n is the affine hyperplane H(p,n) := p + n^perp = {q in A : eta(n,q-p) = 0}; it contains p and is three-dimensional, not a single point. (c) Simultaneity relation. Define q ~_n q' iff eta(n,q'-q) = 0, i.e. iff q'-q lies in n^perp. Then ~_n is an equivalence relation on A whose equivalence classes are exactly the slices H(p,n); reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity are consequences of n^perp being a linear subspace and not physical assumptions. (d) Rest distance. For p,q with q in H(p,n) define d_n(p,q) := sqrt(eta(q-p,q-p)). The integrability question concerns the varying rest distribution p|->n(p)^perp: Frobenius gives local hypersurface leaves tangent to it when its integrability condition holds. Such leaves need not themselves be affine; the affine-plane conclusion requires the additional irrotational Born-rigid hypotheses of the later rigidity theorem. No global foliation is asserted here.

before.title: Counterexample: attainment of the endpoint bound does not force the future time orientation
before.statement: Statement refuted: 'if a piecewise C^1 curve x: [alpha,beta] -> A with nonzero timelike tangents from an event p to an event q attains the endpoint bound sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)) in the length-integral sense, then its tangents must be future timelike, so that it is a worldline of the model'. Counterexample: in an inertial frame with eta = diag(-1,1,1,1) let d := (5,3,0,0), a future timelike displacement with sqrt(-eta(d,d)) = 4, and put p := x^{-1}(0,0,0,0), q := x^{-1}(-5,-3,0,0) = p - d and x(s) := p - s d for s in [0,1]. Then x(0) = p, x(1) = p - d = q, and x'(s) = -d is past timelike for every s, so x is not a future timelike worldline; but its length integrand is sqrt(-eta(-d,-d)) = sqrt(-eta(d,d)) = 4 and its length integral over [0,1] equals 4, while sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)) = sqrt(-eta(-d,-d)) = 4: the bound is attained with equality by a past-directed parametrization. Attainment of the length bound therefore does not force the future time orientation; that orientation enters only through the model's clock interpretation, which attaches readings to future timelike worldlines (def-sr-proper-time, def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline). Within the future timelike worldline class the equality case is characterized by thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum (ii).
before.strategy: Direct computation: eta(-d,-d) = eta(d,d) = -16, so the integrand is the constant 4 and the integral over [0,1] is 4; q - p = -d has the same timelike length. The counterexample isolates exactly the quantifier that fails (attainment does not imply future-directedness); it does not contradict the endpoint-bound theorem, which is stated for future timelike worldlines, and it records why the future hypothesis belongs to the clock reading rather than to the length inequality.

before.title: Observer energy, spatial momentum, invariant mass, rest energy and kinetic energy of a four-momentum
before.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], $c>0$, and let $n\in V$ be future unit, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest space $n^\perp$, rest projection $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$ and norm $|w|=\sqrt{\eta(w,w)}$ on $n^\perp$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c).
(a) For every $P$ in the future closed cone $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ define the observer energy of $P$ relative to $n$ by $E_n(P):=-c\,\eta(P,n)$, the observer spatial momentum by $q_n(P):=h(P)$, and, when $P$ is nonzero future causal, the invariant mass by $m(P):=\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c$. Then $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$, $\eta(n,P)=-E_n(P)/c$, and $P=(E_n(P)/c)\,n+q_n(P)$ is the unique decomposition of $P$ as a multiple of $n$ plus a vector of $n^\perp$; equivalently $E_n$ and $q_n$ are the unique pair of a real number and a vector of $n^\perp$ with that property. For future null $P$ the same formula gives $m(P)=0$.
(b) If $m>0$ and $P$ is written as $P=mU$ with $U$ future timelike and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ (the four-velocity normalisation of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), call $m$ the rest-mass parameter of $P$, $mc^2$ its rest energy and $T_n(P):=E_n(P)-mc^2$ its kinetic energy relative to the observer $n$ and the parameter $m$. The kinetic energy is defined only after $m$ has been fixed, so it is not a function of $P$ and $n$ alone.
(c) The definition claims no positivity of $E_n$, no inequality or vanishing property of $T_n$, and no physical measurement. The names observer energy, spatial momentum, invariant mass, rest energy and kinetic energy and the units joule, kilogram metre per second and kilogram belong to the unit conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and to the physical postulates of this framework; the mathematical content asserted here is only the explicit dependence of the four quantities on $P$, $n$ and $m$.
(d) $E_n$ and $q_n$ are functions of the pair $(P,n)$: $q_n(P)$ is an element of the vector space $V$, not a coordinate triple, and no basis of $V$ enters its definition; $m(P)$ depends on the scalar $\eta(P,P)$ alone; $T_n(P)$ depends additionally on the chosen real number $m$.
before.strategy: Definition item fixing five quantities and their exact dependence. Obligations: (i) $h$ is the linear projection of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c) with image $n^\perp$ and kernel $\mathrm{span}(n)$, so $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$ and the decomposition $P=-\eta(P,n)n+h(P)$ is unique; (ii) $-\eta(P,P)\ge0$ on $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ by [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], so the square root defining $m(P)$ is well defined for every nonzero future causal $P$; (iii) no positivity, monotonicity or measurement statement is imported here — those are supplied by [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]] and by [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]; (iv) $T_n$ is defined only after a rest-mass parameter $m$ is fixed, so it cannot be read as a function of $P$ and $n$ alone. No choice principle is used.

Thus on the future timelike branch $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-c^2m(P)$ is a function of $(P,n)$ alone; no independent choice of $m$ for a fixed admissible $P$ is available.
(c) The definition claims no positivity of $E_n$, no inequality or vanishing property of $T_n$, and no physical measurement. The names observer energy, spatial momentum, invariant mass, rest energy and kinetic energy and the units joule, kilogram metre per second and kilogram belong to the unit conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and to the physical postulates of this framework; the mathematical content asserted here is only the explicit dependence of the four quantities on $P$, $n$ and $m$.
(d) $E_n$ and $q_n$ are functions of the pair $(P,n)$: $q_n(P)$ is an element of the vector space $V$, not a coordinate triple, and no basis of $V$ enters its definition; $m(P)$ depends on the scalar $\eta(P,P)$ alone; $T_n(P)$ in the timelike branch may be presented with $m$, but this parameter is uniquely recovered from $P$ as in(b).
after.strategy: Definition item fixing five quantities and their exact dependence. Obligations: (i) $h$ is the linear projection of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c) with image $n^\perp$ and kernel $\mathrm{span}(n)$, so $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$ and the decomposition $P=-\eta(P,n)n+h(P)$ is unique; (ii) $-\eta(P,P)\ge0$ on $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ by [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], so the square root defining $m(P)$ is well defined for every nonzero future causal $P$; (iii) no positivity, monotonicity or measurement statement is imported here — those are supplied by [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]] and by [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]; (iv) With $P=mU$, $m>0$ and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, bilinearity gives $-\eta(P,P)=m^2c^2$; positivity of $m,c$ and the nonnegative square root give $m=\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c=m(P)$. Therefore the admissible parameter is unique and $T_n$ is a function of $(P,n)$ on this branch. This algebra does not derive physical mass from data; it only identifies the parameter in the specified model. No choice principle is used.

before.title: Worldlines, four-velocity, chart readings and the frame/observer distinction
before.statement: The particle and light objects of the framework are the following curves and vector fields of the affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), with the physical interpretation of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Worldlines] A worldline is a regular causal curve $x:J\to A$ in one of the regularity classes of [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] ($J$ an order-convex subset of $\mathbb R$ with at least two elements). A massive worldline is a $C^k$ future timelike worldline, $k\ge1$, with everywhere nonzero future timelike tangent; a light ray is a $C^1$ future null curve with everywhere nonzero future null tangent. A null curve has zero proper-time increment along every subinterval and no proper-time parametrization ([[def-sr-proper-time]]), and it is never treated as a massive worldline. A worldline is a curve in spacetime; its reading $r\circ x$ in a named laboratory chart is a coordinate description of it, not an object of another observer. (b) [Four-velocity and four-acceleration] For a massive worldline the four-velocity $U$ and, when it is $C^2$, the four-acceleration $A$ are those of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]; wherever defined they satisfy $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and $\eta(U,A)=0$, by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. (c) [Chart reading] If a massive $C^2$ worldline has laboratory reading $t\mapsto r(t)$ in a chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], then $|r'(t)|<c$ for every $t$, with four-velocity $U=\gamma(c,r')$ and Lorentz factor $\gamma=(1-|r'|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, by clause (e) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. (d) [Frames and observers] An inertial frame in this framework is the origin-with-basis object of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]; a point observer is a future unit timelike vector $n\in V$ with rest space $n^\perp$ and rest projection $h$, as in clauses (c)-(d) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. An observer congruence and a noninertial tetrad field are further objects, not defined by this item; the words 'frame', 'chart', 'observer' and 'tetrad' denote distinct notions and are not interchangeable. (e) [Scope] No force law, no self-field and no extended-body structure is supplied here; an accelerating massive worldline requires a force model stated separately, and an ideal light ray carries no dispersive, quantum or polarisation structure in this definition.
before.strategy: A definition reusing the special-relativity curve notions with their exact statements rather than restating them: regularity and causal character of curves are those of [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]; proper time and its non-applicability to null curves are those of [[def-sr-proper-time]]; $U$ and $A$ are those of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]; the identities $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, $\eta(U,A)=0$, the chart bound $|r'|<c$ and the velocity reading $U=\gamma(c,r')$ are the exact clauses of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. The frame/observer distinction is the one of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] together with the rest-space and projection clauses of the same theorem. The item adds the physical interpretation adopted in [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and records the scope exclusions; it proves no dynamical statement.

after.strategy: A definition reusing the special-relativity curve notions with their exact statements rather than restating them: regularity and causal character of curves are those of [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]; proper time and its non-applicability to null curves are those of [[def-sr-proper-time]]; $U$ and $A$ are those of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]; the identities $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, $\eta(U,A)=0$, the chart bound $|r'|<c$ and the velocity reading $U=\gamma(c,r')$ are the exact clauses of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. A nonstraight null trajectory is geometrically admissible: in c=1 chart coordinates x(s)=(s,sin s,-cos s,0) has tangent (1,cos s,sin s,0), which is nonzero future null everywhere, while its spatial direction varies. before.title: Existence, uniqueness and linearity of Fermi-Walker transport
before.statement: Let x: I -> A be a C^2 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U and four-acceleration A, let tau_0 be in I and X_0 in V. Then there is exactly one C^1 field X: I -> V along x with D_FW X/dtau = 0 and X(tau_0) = X_0; if x is C^k with k >= 2 then X is C^{k-1}. The map X_0 |-> X from V to the C^1 fields along x satisfying the transport equation is linear. Consequently, for every tetrad (E_0(tau_0),...,E_3(tau_0)) at x(tau_0) with E_0(tau_0) = U(tau_0)/c there is a unique tuple of Fermi-Walker transported fields with those initial values; whether that tuple remains a tetrad at every time is proved in the following item.
before.strategy: (i) In an inertial chart the equation reads X'^a = M^a{}_b(tau) X^b with M^a{}_b(tau) = c^{-2}(U^a(tau)A_b(tau) - A^a(tau)U_b(tau)), a continuous matrix-valued function on the interval I because x is C^2. (ii) On each compact subinterval [a,b] of I containing tau_0, lem-linear-matrix-odes-have-unique-global-solutions-on-a-given-interval gives a unique solution with the prescribed initial value; uniqueness on overlaps makes the local solutions agree, so they define a unique solution on all of I (I is an increasing union of compact subintervals; equivalently use def-maximal-ode-solution and thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-a-maximal-ode-solution). (iii) Linearity in the initial value follows from uniqueness applied to linear combinations of solutions; the regularity statement follows because the right-hand side M X is C^{k-2} when x is C^k, so the solution gains one derivative. No choice principle is used.

after.title: Existence, uniqueness and linearity of Fermi-Walker transport
after.statement: Let x: I -> A be a C^2 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U and four-acceleration A, let s_0 be in I and X_0 in V. Then there is exactly one C^1 field X: I -> V along x with D_FW X/dtau = 0 and X(s_0) = X_0; if x is C^k with k >= 2 then X is C^{k-1}. The map X_0 |-> X from V to the C^1 fields along x satisfying the transport equation is linear. Consequently, for every tetrad (E_0(s_0),...,E_3(s_0)) at x(s_0) with E_0(s_0) = U(s_0)/c there is a unique tuple of Fermi-Walker transported fields with those initial values; whether that tuple remains a tetrad at every time is proved in the following item.
after.strategy: (i) In an inertial chart the equation reads X'^a(s)=C^a{}_b(s)X^b(s), with C^a{}_b(s)=tau'(s)c^{-2}(U^a(s)A_b(s)-A^a(s)U_b(s)), a continuous matrix-valued function on the given arbitrary interval I because x is C^2 and tau'>0 is C1. To apply the actual matrix-valued ODE supplier to a vector, put X_0 in the first column of a4-by-4 initial matrix and all other columns0; its unique matrix solution has those other columns0 by uniqueness, so the first column solves exactly this vector IVP. (ii) On each compact subinterval [a,b] of I containing s_0, lem-linear-matrix-odes-have-unique-global-solutions-on-a-given-interval gives a unique solution with the prescribed initial value; uniqueness on overlaps makes the local solutions agree, so they define a unique solution on all of I. Explicitly for each s in I the closed segment joining s_0 to s is contained in I; the compact-interval supplier gives its unique solution, and uniqueness on overlapping segments defines the value at s without a choice of solutions from a family. Around any interior s use a compact segment containing a neighbourhood of s and s_0; at an included endpoint use the corresponding one-sided segment. This proves C1 locally, including the defined one-sided endpoints, without assuming that I is open, bounded or a proper-time image. (iii) Linearity in the initial value follows from uniqueness applied to linear combinations of solutions; the regularity statement follows because the right-hand side C X is C^{k-2} when x is C^k, so the solution gains one derivative. No choice principle is used.

before.title: Counterexample: simultaneity is relative to the observer vector
before.statement: Statement refuted: 'the simultaneity relation eta(n,q-p) = 0 between events of the affine model is independent of the future unit timelike vector n.' Counterexample: in an inertial chart let p := x^{-1}(0,0,0,0) and q := x^{-1}(0,1,0,0), so d := q - p is spacelike with eta(d,d) = 1, and let n := e_0 = (1,0,0,0) and n' := gamma(e_0 + (3/5)e_1) = (5/4)(1,3/5,0,0), a boost of speed 3c/5 along the first axis; n' is future unit because eta(n',n') = (25/16)(-1 + 9/25) = -1. Then eta(n,d) = 0, so p and q are simultaneous relative to n and lie in the slice H(p,n), while eta(n',d) = (5/4)(3/5) = 3/4 is nonzero, so p and q are not simultaneous relative to n' and lie in different slices for n'. The two slices H(p,n) and H(p,n') are distinct three-dimensional affine hyperplanes through p. Hence simultaneity in the sense of def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance depends on the observer vector, so it is not an observer-independent relation.
before.strategy: Exact rational evaluation of eta on the displayed vectors; both n and n' are verified future unit by the diagonal form, and the two pairings with d are computed exactly (0 and 3/4). The slices are distinct because their direction subspaces n^perp and n'^perp differ (the vector e_1 - (3/5)e_0 lies in the first but not in the second).

before.title: Null wave covectors, frame frequency data and the observer frequency of an ideal plane wave
before.statement: Adopt the SI coordinate and unit conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions: in every inertial chart x^0 = c t with c > 0 in metres per second and spatial coordinates in metres, so c is the model's conversion constant. Let k be a future null wave covector and theta its affine phase (def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector). (a) Frame data as wave data. In the inertial chart of a frame let (varpi,s) be the frame data of lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data, so varpi = -k(e_0) > 0 and |s| = 1. Define the angular frequency omega := c varpi (unit s^-1), the linear frequency nu := omega/(2 pi) (unit s^-1, hertz), the wave vector kappa := (omega/c) s (unit m^-1; |kappa| = omega/c), the wavelength lambda := 2 pi/|kappa| = 2 pi c/omega = c/nu (unit m), and the propagation direction s (dimensionless). In these conventions the phase is theta(p) = -omega t + kappa . x_vec(p) + const with t := x^0(p)/c the coordinate time in seconds, so the components of k in the chart are k_a = (-omega/c, (omega/c)s_1, (omega/c)s_2, (omega/c)s_3). (b) Observer frequency. For an ideal observer whose four-velocity is U_o = c n with n in V future unit timelike (eta(n,n) = -1; def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition) define the observer angular frequency of the wave as omega_n := -c k(n) = -k(U_o) in s^-1, and the observer linear frequency as omega_n/(2 pi); by lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline this is minus the rate of change of the phase with respect to the observer's own proper time, and the sign convention makes it positive. (c) Well-definedness. varpi = -k(e_0) > 0 and |s| = 1 in every inertial frame (frame-data lemma), hence omega > 0 and lambda > 0 are well defined and independent of the choices made in their computation; omega_n > 0 for every future unit timelike n and every future null wave covector (lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative), so every ideal observer reads a positive angular frequency; omega_n depends only on k and the observer vector n. (d) This item fixes definitions, units and sign conventions only. It does not assert that any physical light is described by such a phase; that identification is adopted in post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model. It contains no quantum identification of energy with hbar omega, no amplitude or intensity content, no medium or dispersion model, no source or detector model and no measurement or empirical claim.
before.strategy: Formulation obligations, not a proof of a physical claim. (a) The definitions are functions of k and the frame; well-definedness of varpi and s is lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data and the SI conversion is def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions, so the physical names attached to the mathematical numbers are a convention fixed here. The relation theta(p) = -omega t + kappa . x_vec(p) + const is the substitution x^0 = c t in k_a x^a. (b) n = U_o/c is future unit timelike by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition(a); omega_n = -c k(n) = -k(U_o) by linearity; positivity and the proper-time-derivative reading are lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative and lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline with the sign convention explicitly chosen here. (c) Positivity and frame-independence are the quoted lemmas. (d) The scope clause records that the physical interpretation (light is described by an ideal plane wave, and the number defined here is the frequency an ideal observer reads) is adopted only in post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model; the definition item must not be presented as implying it. No proof of a physical claim is manufactured; no choice principle is used.

before.title: Total four-momentum, invariant mass and center-of-momentum frame of a finite system
before.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model and $c>0$.
(a) For a finite list $(P_1,\dots,P_N)$, $N\ge0$, of vectors of $V$ define the total four-momentum $P_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\sum_{i=1}^NP_i$ as the finite sum of [[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]] in the additive group $(V,+)$; the empty sum is $0$.
(b) If $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future timelike, define its invariant mass $M:=M(P_{\mathrm{tot}}):=\sqrt{-\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},P_{\mathrm{tot}})}/c>0$ and its rest energy $Mc^2$; if $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future null, set $M:=0$ and say that the system has no rest frame. For zero, spacelike or past $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ this convention defines no invariant mass.
(c) A center-of-momentum frame of a nonzero $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ whose first vector satisfies $q_{e_0}(P_{\mathrm{tot}})=0$, i.e. the total spatial momentum vanishes for the frame's stationary observer; by [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] this is equivalent to $P_{\mathrm{tot}}=-\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},e_0)e_0$, that is, to $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ being a positive multiple of $e_0$.
(d) The invariant mass of a single future timelike vector $P$ coincides with $m(P)$ of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; in particular for $P=mU$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ it equals $m$.
(e) No existence of a center-of-momentum frame, no physical conservation law and no dynamics are asserted by this definition; position, event and simultaneity data do not enter $\sum_iP_i$, and only the total vector carries the invariant mass.
before.strategy: Definition item. after.title: Total four-momentum, invariant mass and center-of-momentum frame of a finite system
after.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model and $c>0$.
(a) For a finite list $(P_1,\dots,P_N)$, $N\ge0$, of vectors of $V$ define the total four-momentum $P_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\sum_{i=1}^NP_i$ as the finite sum of [[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]] in the additive group $(V,+)$; the empty sum is $0$.
(b) If $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future timelike, define its invariant mass $M:=M(P_{\mathrm{tot}}):=\sqrt{-\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},P_{\mathrm{tot}})}/c>0$ and its rest energy $Mc^2$; if $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future null, set $M:=0$ and say that the system has no rest frame. For zero, spacelike or past $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ this convention defines no invariant mass.
(c) A center-of-momentum frame of a nonzero $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ whose first vector satisfies $q_{e_0}(P_{\mathrm{tot}})=0$, i.e. the total spatial momentum vanishes for the frame's stationary observer; by [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] this is equivalent to $P_{\mathrm{tot}}=-\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},e_0)e_0$, that is, to $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ being a nonzero real multiple of $e_0$. This multiple is positive precisely when $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future timelike, and negative precisely when it is past timelike; the arbitrary nonzero-vector convention in this clause is retained.
(d) The invariant mass of a single future timelike vector $P$ coincides with $m(P)$ of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; in particular for $P=mU$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ it equals $m$.
(e) No existence of a center-of-momentum frame, no physical conservation law and no dynamics are asserted by this definition; position, event and simultaneity data do not enter $\sum_iP_i$, and only the total vector carries the invariant mass.

before.title: Positivity, mass shell and kinetic energy of the observer quantities of a four-momentum
before.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, $n$ future unit, and let $E_n,q_n,m,T_n$ be the quantities of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]].
(a) If $P$ is nonzero future causal, then $E_n(P)>0$, $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$ and
$$\eta(q_n(P),q_n(P))=\frac{E_n(P)^2}{c^2}+\eta(P,P)\ \ge\ 0 .$$
Consequently: (i) if $P$ is future null then $\eta(P,P)=0$ and $E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$; (ii) if $P$ is future timelike with invariant mass $m(P)$ then $\eta(P,P)=-m(P)^2c^2$ and the mass-shell identity
$$E_n(P)^2=m(P)^2c^4+c^2\,|q_n(P)|^2$$
holds. The invariant mass $m(P)$ does not depend on the observer $n$ or on coordinates, being a function of the scalar $\eta(P,P)$ alone, while $E_n$ and $q_n$ do depend on $n$.
(b) Let $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant and $U$ future timelike, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. With $\gamma:=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$ and $w:=c\,h(U)/\gamma\in n^\perp$ the relative velocity of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d), one has
$$E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma,\qquad T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)\ \ge\ 0,\qquad q_n(P)=m\gamma w,$$
and $m(P)=m$. Moreover $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if $\gamma=1$, that is $U=cn$, equivalently $P=mcn$ (the particle is at rest relative to $n$). Finally $|q_n(P)|=m\gamma|w|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}$.
before.strategy: All clauses are algebra in the flat model. (a) Expand $q_n(P)=P+\eta(P,n)n$: bilinearity and $\eta(n,n)=-1$ give $\eta(q_n,q_n)=\eta(P,P)+\eta(P,n)^2$, and $\eta(P,n)=-E_n(P)/c$. Positivity of $E_n$: choose an $\eta$-orthonormal basis with first vector in $C^+$ ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]], [[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]]) and write $P=P^0e_0+P_s$, $n=n^0e_0+n_s$; then $n^0>|n_s|$ and $P^0\ge|P_s|$ by [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], so $-\eta(P,n)=P^0n^0-P_s\cdot n_s\ge n^0|P_s|-|n_s|\,|P_s|=|P_s|(n^0-|n_s|)\ge0$ using the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]); equality forces $P_s=0$, and then $P\ne0$ gives $P^0>0$ and $-\eta(P,n)=P^0n^0>0$. Substitute $\eta(P,P)=-m(P)^2c^2$ for (ii). (b) From $u:=U/c=\gamma(n+w/c)$ of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d) one gets $q_n(P)=mc\,h(u)=m\gamma w$ and $E_n(P)=-mc\,\eta(U,n)=mc^2(-\eta(U/c,n))=mc^2\gamma$; the rest is the identity $|w|^2=c^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$ and $\gamma\ge1$ from the same item, with $\gamma=1$ if and only if $u=n$. No choice principle is used.

before.title: Proper acceleration of a massive worldline and its agreement with the acceleration of an observer congruence
before.statement: Let c > 0 and let x: I -> A be a C^2 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U = dx/dtau and four-acceleration A = dU/dtau (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration), so that eta(U,U) = -c^2 and eta(U,A) = 0 pointwise, and A(tau) is spacelike whenever it is nonzero (thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a),(b)). (a) Definition. The proper acceleration of x at the parameter value tau is the real number a(tau) := sqrt(eta(A(tau),A(tau))), the nonnegative square root of def-rational-power. This is well defined for every tau in I: if A(tau) = 0 then eta(A,A) = 0, and if A(tau) is nonzero then it is spacelike and eta(A,A) > 0 (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors); in both cases the argument of the square root is nonnegative, so a(tau) is a nonnegative real number. With the SI coordinate and unit conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions, in which x^0 = c t with t in seconds and the spatial coordinates are in metres while eta has the dimensionless matrix diag(-1,1,1,1) in an inertial chart, the components of A carry the unit metre per second squared and eta(A,A) carries the unit (metre per second squared)^2, so a carries the unit metre per second squared. The worldline is uniformly accelerated when a is constant on I. (b) Agreement with the acceleration of a congruence. Let Omega be a nonempty open subset of A and let n: Omega -> V be an observer congruence with acceleration field a_cg := nabla_n n, where nabla is the flat covariant derivative of def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (b)). If x is a flow line of n and U = c n along x, then A = c^2 a_cg along x, and consequently a = c^2 sqrt(eta(a_cg,a_cg)) along x: the proper acceleration is c^2 times the magnitude of the congruence acceleration. In particular the proper acceleration of a congruence worldline is determined by the congruence field alone, and such a worldline is uniformly accelerated exactly when eta(a_cg,a_cg) is constant along it. (c) Reading and scope. This item defines a quantity of the model and fixes its name, its unit and its physical reading. The model reads a(tau) as the magnitude that an ideal accelerometer carried along the worldline would register at tau; this ideal-instrument identification is adopted with the model in the same sense as the framework's ideal-clock reading of proper time and is not derived here. No accelerometer response law, calibration, frequency dependence, force law or interaction is specified or asserted; the definition asserts nothing about which bodies follow which worldlines; no measurement outcome and no statistical, uncertainty or empirical claim is made. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Definition with its well-definedness and its unit and congruence clauses justified by the cited suppliers. (a) A is continuous because x is C^2 (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration (b)); eta(A,A) is the sum of products of continuous component functions in any inertial chart (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart, thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions); eta(A,A) >= 0 pointwise by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (b) together with the classification of nonzero spacelike vectors by def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors. Hence sqrt(eta(A,A)) is well defined for every tau as the nonnegative real whose square is eta(A,A) (def-rational-power). Units are read off directly from def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions, which lists the unit metre per second squared for the four-acceleration and the dimensionless matrix diag(-1,1,1,1) for eta in an inertial chart. (b) If U = c n along x with c a constant, then A = dU/dtau = c d(n o x)/dtau; the derivative of the field n along the worldline is the covariant derivative nabla_{dx/dtau} n = nabla_{cn} n = c nabla_n n = c a_cg by the defining properties of the flat covariant derivative along curves (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (d)); hence A = c^2 a_cg and eta(A,A) = c^4 eta(a_cg,a_cg), so a = c^2 sqrt(eta(a_cg,a_cg)) because c > 0. The acceleration a_cg is spacelike or zero by def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (b), so eta(a_cg,a_cg) >= 0. (c) The scope clause records that the accelerometer reading is an ideal-instrument identification of the model and that no apparatus, force or measurement model is asserted; this mirrors the treatment of clock readings in post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and of wave frequencies in def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency. No choice principle is used.

before.title: The microscopic vacuum Maxwell equations: smooth and weak branches
before.statement:
Adopt as a physical postulate of this framework the following four equations for the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the sources of [[def-em-sources]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^1$ fields with the additional derivatives required by each equation existing and continuous, and let $\rho,J$ be continuous. Then, with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

after.title: The microscopic vacuum Maxwell equations: smooth and weak branches
after.statement:
Adopt as a physical postulate of this framework the following four equations for the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the sources of [[def-em-sources]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^1$ fields with the additional derivatives required by each equation existing and continuous, and let $\rho,J$ be continuous. Then, with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

(b) [Weak branch] Let instead $E,B$ be locally integrable $\mathbb R^3$-valued fields and $\rho,J$ locally integrable scalar and vector fields on $I\times\Omega$, paired with tests by their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]). For each given locally integrable component this pairing and its order-zero continuity are choice-free: on compact K its absolute value is bounded by sup_K|psi| times the finite integral of its absolute value, and [[thm-local-finite-order-characterization-of-distributions]] applies. The further identification as a faithful embedding of almost-everywhere equivalence classes, and the strong local-L1 embedding interface of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], use exactly its additional assumption of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]); they are not prerequisites for merely writing the given-L1 weak pairings. Let $\operatorname{div}$, $\operatorname{curl}$ and $\partial_t$ act as distributional derivatives, and let $\psi$ range over $C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]). Then the same four identities hold in the sense of [[def-distribution]]: the pairings $\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle$ and $\langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$ vanish for every such $\psi$, all derivatives being distributional derivatives ([[def-distributional-derivative]]). (c) [Scope] The postulate contains no magnetic charge: $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and no magnetic-source term appears in $\operatorname{curl}E$. Sources that are not locally integrable functions (point or sheet sources) are covered by neither branch and require their own definition. The equations are adopted classical vacuum physics in the named inertial chart; they are not deduced from charge conservation, from empirical agreement or from the special-relativity postulates, and this item by itself asserts no covariance under changes of inertial frame.

The compact-support absolute-integral bound and the choice-free local finite-order criterion prove continuity without invoking injectivity. Only a faithful a.e.-quotient identification invokes the Countable Choice assumption of the actual embedding theorem; the smooth and given-L1 pairing branches do not acquire that extra premise. before.title: Radar synchronization of an inertial observer reproduces its inertial chart
before.statement: Adopt post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light (ideal clocks read proper time; ideal vacuum light rays are exactly the future null straight lines) and the SI conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame with chart x, put n := e_0 (future unit, eta(n,n) = -1) and let W := x^{-1}({(lambda,0,0,0) : lambda in R}) be the coordinate axis, a straight future timelike worldline whose proper time between the events with coordinates (lambda_-,0,0,0) and (lambda_+,0,0,0) is (lambda_+ - lambda_-)/c up to an additive constant (def-sr-proper-time). Let q be an event whose spatial coordinates r := (x^1(q),x^2(q),x^3(q)) are nonzero, and put lambda_± := x^0(q) ± |r| with |r| the Euclidean norm of def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame. Then: (i) the events e_- := x^{-1}(lambda_-,0,0,0) and e_+ := x^{-1}(lambda_+,0,0,0) lie on W, and q - e_-, e_+ - q are future null; hence the radar protocol of def-sr-operational-radar-protocol applies with emission e_-, reflection q and reception e_+; (ii) the radar assignments are tau_rad(q) = x^0(q)/c and rho_rad(q) = |r| up to the additive constant of the observer's proper time: the radar time is the chart time of q and the radar distance is the chart's rest-frame distance; (iii) consequently, on the region of events with nonzero spatial part, radar simultaneity of this observer coincides with chart simultaneity (equal radar times are equal x^0), and the radar distance equals the rest distance in the simultaneity slice H(m,n) of the midpoint event m := x^{-1}(x^0(q),0,0,0); (iv) scope and qualification: this is a conditional statement of the adopted ideal model, showing that the operational round-trip protocol reproduces the inertial chart's time and rest distance, so the operational content of inertial simultaneity is this two-way radar convention; it asserts no one-way light-speed measurement without a synchronization convention, no empirical calibration, no result for accelerated, rotating or dispersive situations, and no deviation from the model. The idealizations of the postulates are carried into the conclusion.
before.strategy: Conditional deduction from the adopted premises. The geometry is lem-sr-radar-midpoint-for-inertial-observer with o := x^{-1}(0,0,0,0), n := e_0 and lambda_± := x^0(q) ± |r|: the events e_± are exactly o + lambda_± n, and the displacement q - o = x^0(q) n + r_vec decomposes as -eta(n,q-o) n + h(q-o) with -eta(n,q-o) = x^0(q) and |h(q-o)| = |r| in the chart coordinates (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame), so |u| = |r| = (lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2 and the lemma gives q - e_-, e_+ - q future null. By post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light the clock reads tau and the two segments are traversed by ideal rays, so the protocol's assignments of def-sr-operational-radar-protocol apply, and they equal tau_rad(q) = (lambda_- + lambda_+)/(2c) = x^0(q)/c and rho_rad(q) = (lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2 = |r|. Clause (iii) restates this as equality of radar times and x^0; the midpoint event m is the orthogonal projection of q onto W. The scope clause records that the statement is conditional on the ideal postulates and carries no empirical claim; no choice principle is used.
before.physical_scope: Ideal radar synchronization of a single inertial observer in flat classical special-relativistic spacetime, conditional on the ideal-clock and ideal-light postulates and the SI coordinate conventions: the round-trip protocol reproduces the observer's inertial chart time and rest-frame distance. Excludes one-way synchronization claims without an explicit convention, accelerated or rotating observers, dispersive media, real clock and light imperfections, detector models, and all empirical and statistical claims.

before.title: Fermi-Walker transport preserves the metric, and explicit rigid and non-rigid observer congruences
before.statement: (a) Preservation. Let x: I -> A be a C^2 future timelike worldline and let X,Y: I -> V be C^1 Fermi-Walker transported fields along x (def-sr-fermi-walker-transport). Then tau |-> eta(X(tau),Y(tau)) is constant on I; in particular Fermi-Walker transport preserves norms and orthogonality, and the unique Fermi-Walker transported family with initial values a tetrad (E_0(tau_0),...,E_3(tau_0)) with E_0(tau_0) = U(tau_0)/c is an orthonormal tetrad (E_0(tau),...,E_3(tau)) at every tau with E_0(tau) = U(tau)/c (observer-adapted tetrad), by lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness. (b) Rindler wedge congruence. In an inertial chart (x^0,x,y,z) consider Phi(theta,rho,y,z) := (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) on R x (0,inf) x R^2, with theta in R and rho>0. Then Phi is a smooth bijection onto the right wedge W := {(x^0,x) : x > |x^0|}, with smooth inverse rho = sqrt(x^2 - (x^0)^2), theta = (1/2) log((x + x^0)/(x - x^0)); the pullback of eta is g = -rho^2 d theta^2 + d rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2; the field n := rho^{-1} partial/partial theta is a future unit timelike field on W whose congruence is Born rigid and irrotational, with acceleration a = nabla_n n = rho^{-1} partial/partial rho, hence eta(a,a) = rho^{-2}; its rest slices theta = const are hyperplanes orthogonal to n with induced metric d rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 independent of theta; and the frame (n, partial/partial rho, partial/partial y, partial/partial z) is a tetrad field which is not a coordinate frame, since [n, partial/partial rho] = +(1/rho) n is nonzero (def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields). (c) Rigid rotation, ambient nonintegrability and ring holonomy. Fix real Omega. In the inertial chart let U_Omega be the open timelike region r^2=(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2<c^2/Omega^2 when Omega!=0, and the whole chart when Omega=0. On this four-dimensional open set put K=partial_0+(Omega/c)(-x^2 partial_1+x^1 partial_2), gamma(r)=(1-Omega^2 r^2/c^2)^(-1/2), and n=gamma(r)K. This is a smooth future unit timelike Born-rigid congruence. If Omega!=0, its three-dimensional rest distribution in the ambient open set is nowhere integrable: its vorticity is nowhere zero and no ambient rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists locally. If Omega=0, n=partial_0 is inertial and irrotational, and the rest hypersurfaces are x^0=const. Now fix R>0 with |Omega|R<c and restrict to the timelike ring cylinder r=R, x^3=const, whose rotating angle is varphi=phi-Omega t modulo2pi, x^0=ct. The ring observer phi=phi_0+Omega t has n=gamma(R)(1,-(Omega R/c)sin phi,(Omega R/c)cos phi,0). The induced metric is -(c^2-Omega^2R^2)dt^2+2Omega R^2 dt dvarphi+R^2 dvarphi^2. The ambient rest covector restricted to the cylinder is proportional to -(c^2-Omega^2R^2)dt+Omega R^2 dvarphi, so the one-dimensional rest distribution on that cylinder is locally integrable and satisfies dt/dvarphi=Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2). After one positive circuit in the rotating label, its lift starting at t=0 has signed time offset Delta t=2pi Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2). For Omega!=0 it returns to the same rotating label at a different time and does not close as a ring rest-simultaneity curve; there is no globally single-valued real rest-synchronization time on the entire cylinder with time-oriented nonzero differential annihilating these rest lines. This global ring holonomy is distinct from the ambient local Frobenius obstruction. For Omega=0 the offset is zero and ring rest lines are t=const. (d) Bell first-order field. Let q: J -> R^3 be C^2 with q(t) = (q_1(t),0,0) and |q_1'(t)| < c, and consider the C1 future unit field of the translated worldlines x_xi(t) = (c t, q(t) + xi) parametrized by xi in an open subset of R^3, with n = gamma(1, q_1'(t)/c, 0, 0), gamma = (1 - q_1'(t)^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and unit longitudinal rest vector s = gamma(q_1'(t)/c, 1, 0, 0). For this C1 field define the first-order rest projection $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$ and projected deformation $\theta_{ab}=h^c{}_a h^d{}_b\partial_{(c}n_{d)}$, using the explicit first-order version of def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space. These coordinate formulas need only C1 n, give a continuous tensor, and agree with the smooth congruence definitions when q is smooth; in this first-order sense Born rigidity means theta=0. Then theta(s,s) = s^a s^b partial_a n_b = gamma^3 q_1'(t) q_1''(t)/c^3, which is nonzero exactly when q_1'(t) q_1''(t) is nonzero; hence the congruence is not Born rigid on any neighbourhood of a parameter value with q_1'(t) q_1''(t) nonzero, although for every fixed chart time t the separation between the members labelled xi_1 and xi_2 is the constant |xi_1 - xi_2|. A breaking or fracture conclusion about a material rod would additionally require an elasticity model and a failure criterion and is not a kinematic statement.
before.strategy: (a) For Fermi-Walker transported X,Y, d/dtau eta(X,Y) = eta(X',Y) + eta(X,Y') and substituting X' = c^{-2}(eta(A,X)U - eta(U,X)A) and the analogous expression for Y' gives c^{-2}[eta(A,X)eta(U,Y) - eta(U,X)eta(A,Y) + eta(A,Y)eta(U,X) - eta(U,Y)eta(A,X)] = 0. The initial-tetrad family therefore remains orthonormal, and E_0 = U/c is transported by def-sr-fermi-walker-transport (b); uniqueness is lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness. (b) Injectivity of Phi follows from x^2 - (x^0)^2 = rho^2 and the sign of x; the inverse formulas are the standard hyperbolic identities cosh^2 - sinh^2 = 1 and tanh(theta) = x^0/x, and both maps are smooth on their domains because rho > 0 and x - x^0 > 0. Differentiating Phi gives dx^0 = sinh theta d rho + rho cosh theta d theta, dx = cosh theta d rho + rho sinh theta d theta, so -(dx^0)^2 + dx^2 = -rho^2 d theta^2 + d rho^2. The field n is unit future by inspection; a direct computation with the metric gives nabla_{partial_theta} partial_theta = rho partial_rho and hence a = nabla_n n = rho^{-1} partial_rho; the rest slices are the theta-level sets, orthogonal to n because the metric has no theta-rho cross term, with the displayed induced metric independent of theta, so theta_{ab} = 0 and, since the slice is orthogonal to a field whose rest distribution is integrable, omega = 0; the commutator is [rho^{-1}partial_theta, partial_rho] = +(1/rho^2)partial_theta = +(1/rho)n. (c) K is future timelike exactly on the stated U_Omega and is Killing by direct coordinate differentiation. after.title: Fermi-Walker transport preserves the metric, and explicit rigid and non-rigid observer congruences

before.title: The smooth local Herglotz-Noether classification of Born-rigid motions
before.statement: Let n be a smooth future unit timelike field on a nonempty open subset Omega of A with acceleration a = nabla_n n, rest metric h, expansion theta and vorticity omega, and assume that n is Born rigid, theta = 0 (def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics). (i) Preliminary identity. For every smooth vector field X on Omega with eta(n,X) = 0 one has nabla_X n = 0 if and only if theta(X,.) = 0 and omega(X,.) = 0; in particular, if theta = omega = 0 on an open set U then nabla_X n = 0 for every vector field X on U tangent to the rest distribution. (ii) Rotational case. Suppose omega is nowhere zero on a flow box U with adapted coordinates (s,y) and n = partial_s (thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius). Then the vorticity and the acceleration are basic (their components in the adapted coframe do not depend on s), d(a-flat) = 0 on U, and for any primitive F of the closed one-form a-flat on the star-shaped box U (thm-poincare-lemma-for-differential-forms-on-star-shaped-domains) the field K := exp(F) n is a timelike Killing field, nabla_a K_b + nabla_b K_a = 0, equivalently L_K eta = 0; if U is connected and simply connected with omega nowhere zero, a single positive smooth f on U satisfies L_{f n} eta = 0 (lem-sr-closed-one-form-primitive-on-simply-connected-open-sets). Conversely every future timelike Killing field on a connected open set, normalized as n = K/sqrt(-eta(K,K)), is Born rigid, and its flow is rotational exactly when its vorticity is nowhere zero. (iii) Irrotational case. Suppose theta = omega = 0 on Omega. Then on a sufficiently small neighbourhood U of every point the connected leaves of the rest distribution are open subsets of affine hyperplanes: there are a smooth future timelike curve z: J -> A with eta(z',z') = -1 and a smooth function sigma: U -> J such that, in the sense of the unique label, the leaves are the hyperplanes H_s = z(s) + z'(s)^perp, n = z' o sigma on U, N(x)=1+eta(z''(sigma(x)),x-z(sigma(x)))>0, d sigma(v)=-eta(z'(sigma(x)),v)/N(x), a = (z'' o sigma)/N, and nabla n = dsigma (x) (z'' o sigma); the tubular label has derivative 1 + eta(z'' o sigma, x - z o sigma), which is nonzero (taken positive) on U. Conversely, for every smooth future timelike curve z with eta(z',z') = -1 the field n := z' o sigma on any tubular neighbourhood on which the label sigma is unique with positive derivative is a smooth irrotational Born-rigid congruence with these same formulas. (iv) Scope. All statements are local on Omega; no global classification of rigid motions, no global orbit quotient, no completeness and no global restriction on the size of a rigid body is asserted beyond what the local formulas give. The rotational case is the local form of the Herglotz-Noether statement that a rotational Born-rigid motion is Killing; the irrotational case describes the orthogonal affine-plane families.
before.strategy: The proof follows the research argument in research/first-principles-2026-10-03/relativity/scaffold/sr-supplier-proofs.md S11, which supplies the calculational omissions of Giulini, math-ph/0602018, Section 5.5 pp. 41-49, and avoids both the source's analyticity assumption and its unsafe global orbit quotient. (i) For horizontal X the decomposition gives nabla_X n_b = theta(X,.) + omega(X,.), so vanishing of both is equivalent to nabla_X n = 0. (ii) In adapted coordinates (s,y) with n = partial_s one has h_{ss} = h_{si} = 0, the slice metric h_ij(y) is independent of s by Born rigidity, and one chooses an orthonormal coframe theta^i of the slice metric (thm-gram-schmidt-orthonormalisation), pulled back to the box, together with theta^0 = -n-flat; then g = -(theta^0)^2 + sum (theta^i)^2. Writing a = a_i theta^i and omega = (1/2)omega_ij theta^i wedge theta^j, the kinematic decomposition gives d theta^0 = -theta^0 wedge a - 2 omega and d theta^i = -gamma-bar^i_j wedge theta^j, where gamma-bar is the pullback of the Levi-Civita connection of the slice metric (thm-fundamental-theorem-of-riemannian-geometry). The connection 1-forms of the flat connection in this coframe are gamma^0_i = gamma^i_0 = a_i theta^0 - omega_ij theta^j and gamma^i_j = gamma-bar^i_j - omega_ij theta^0; substituting into the structure equations verifies d theta^A = -gamma^A_B wedge theta^B and the Lorentz skew conditions, and the flatness identity d gamma + gamma wedge gamma = 0 (zero curvature of def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space) has horizontal components 0 = R-bar_ijkl + 2omega_ij omega_kl + omega_ik omega_jl - omega_il omega_jk and 0 = D_k omega_ij - D_j omega_ik - 2 a_i omega_jk, where R-bar is the curvature four-tensor of the slice metric (def-riemann-curvature-four-tensor) and D the slice covariant derivative. In three dimensions the four-form component identity omega_ij omega_kl - omega_ik omega_jl + omega_il omega_jk = 0 holds, so R-bar_ijkl = -3 omega_ij omega_kl. Since h is s-independent, R-bar is basic; differentiating R-bar = -3 omega (x) omega along n gives n(omega_ij) omega_kl + omega_ij n(omega_kl) = 0, whence n(omega_kl) = 0 for every pair with omega_kl nonzero and then n(omega_ij) = 0 for all pairs: omega is basic. Differentiating the second relation along n (the frame and D are basic) gives omega_jk n(a_i) = 0, so a is basic. Applying d^2 = 0 to theta^0 (thm-the-exterior-derivative-squares-to-zero) gives 0 = 2 omega wedge a + theta^0 wedge da - 2 d omega; Cartan's formula gives i_n d omega=L_n omega-d(i_n omega)=0 since omega is basic and horizontal. Contracting the displayed identity with n, using theta^0(n)=1 and i_n omega=i_n a=0, gives da-theta^0 wedge i_n da=0, hence the horizontal part of da vanishes. Likewise i_n da=L_n a-d(i_n a)=0 because a is basic and horizontal; therefore da=0. No horizontal projection of theta^0 wedge da is used to infer this. On the star-shaped box the Poincare lemma gives a-flat = dF; with f = exp(F) one computes L_{f n} eta = f L_n eta + df (x) n-flat + n-flat (x) df = -f(n-flat (x) a + a (x) n-flat) + f a (x) n-flat + f n-flat (x) a = 0 using L_n eta = -(n-flat (x) a + a (x) n-flat) and a = dF = d log f, so K = f n is Killing. The global simply connected version replaces the star-shaped primitive by the path-integral primitive of lem-sr-closed-one-form-primitive-on-simply-connected-open-sets. The converse is immediate from L_K eta = 0 and (L_{fn}eta) = f L_n eta + df (x) n-flat + n-flat (x) df. (iii) With theta = omega = 0, (i) gives nabla_X n = 0 for leaf-tangent X; on a connected leaf n is therefore constant (the ambient parallel transport is trivial and the leaf is connected), so the leaf's tangent space is the fixed subspace n^perp and integrating the constant tangent shows the leaf lies in the affine hyperplane through any of its points with direction n^perp. Choose a flow line z(s) with z' = n; the leaf through z(s) is z(s) + z'(s)^perp. The label function sigma is obtained from the implicit function theorem (thm-implicit-function-theorem-for-banach-spaces) applied to (s,x) |-> eta(z'(s), x - z(s)), whose s-derivative is 1 + eta(z''(s), x - z(s)) and equals 1 at x = z(s); implicit differentiation gives d sigma(v)=-eta(z'(sigma),v)/N and therefore n(sigma)=1/N; the field derivative is nabla n=d sigma (x) z''(sigma), and its acceleration is nabla_n n=z''(sigma)/N, not z''(sigma) away from the centre curve. These same formulas verify the converse: sigma-level sets are affine hyperplanes, n is constant along each leaf, so theta=omega=0. The positivity of N fixes the future-oriented tubular label. No choice principle is used; all objects are finite-dimensional and the cited ODE/flow suppliers are those of the published mathematics library.

The connection 1-forms of the flat connection in this coframe are gamma^0_i = gamma^i_0 = a_i theta^0 - omega_ij theta^j and gamma^i_j = gamma-bar^i_j - omega_ij theta^0; substituting into the structure equations verifies d theta^A = -gamma^A_B wedge theta^B and the Lorentz skew conditions, and the flatness identity d gamma + gamma wedge gamma = 0 (zero curvature of def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space) has horizontal components 0 = R-bar_ijkl + 2omega_ij omega_kl + omega_ik omega_jl - omega_il omega_jk and 0 = D_k omega_ij - D_j omega_ik - 2 a_i omega_jk, where R-bar_ijkl:=Rm(e_k,e_l,e_j,e_i) is the connection-form coefficient convention, and D is the slice covariant derivative. Here the published def-riemann-curvature-four-tensor uses Rm(X,Y,Z,W)=h(R(X,Y)Z,W), so its same-order Rm(e_i,e_j,e_k,e_l) is not R-bar_ijkl. Indeed the curvature 2-form Omega-bar^i_j(e_k,e_l) equals h(R(e_k,e_l)e_j,e_i), precisely the displayed permutation. All subsequent R-bar contractions use this convention; for example R-bar_1212=-3 omega_12^2 corresponds to Rm(e_1,e_2,e_1,e_2)=+3 omega_12^2, because the last two curvature slots are skew. The slice metric is unchanged, and the basicness argument uses this fixed permutation, not a sign change of Rm. In three dimensions the four-form component identity omega_ij omega_kl - omega_ik omega_jl + omega_il omega_jk = 0 holds, so R-bar_ijkl = -3 omega_ij omega_kl. Since h is s-independent, R-bar is basic; differentiating R-bar = -3 omega (x) omega along n gives n(omega_ij) omega_kl + omega_ij n(omega_kl) = 0, whence n(omega_kl) = 0 for every pair with omega_kl nonzero and then n(omega_ij) = 0 for all pairs: omega is basic. Differentiating the second relation along n (the frame and D are basic) gives omega_jk n(a_i) = 0, so a is basic. Applying d^2 = 0 to theta^0 (thm-the-exterior-derivative-squares-to-zero) gives 0 = 2 omega wedge a + theta^0 wedge da - 2 d omega; Cartan's formula gives i_n d omega=L_n omega-d(i_n omega)=0 since omega is basic and horizontal. Contracting the displayed identity with n, using theta^0(n)=1 and i_n omega=i_n a=0, gives da-theta^0 wedge i_n da=0, hence the horizontal part of da vanishes. Likewise i_n da=L_n a-d(i_n a)=0 because a is basic and horizontal; therefore da=0. No horizontal projection of theta^0 wedge da is used to infer this. On the star-shaped box the Poincare lemma gives a-flat = dF; with f = exp(F) one computes L_{f n} eta = f L_n eta + df (x) n-flat + n-flat (x) df = -f(n-flat (x) a + a (x) n-flat) + f a (x) n-flat + f n-flat (x) a = 0 using L_n eta = -(n-flat (x) a + a (x) n-flat) and a = dF = d log f, so K = f n is Killing. The global simply connected version replaces the star-shaped primitive by the path-integral primitive of lem-sr-closed-one-form-primitive-on-simply-connected-open-sets. The converse is immediate from L_K eta = 0 and (L_{fn}eta) = f L_n eta + df (x) n-flat + n-flat (x) df. (iii) With theta = omega = 0, (i) gives nabla_X n = 0 for leaf-tangent X; on a connected leaf n is therefore constant (the ambient parallel transport is trivial and the leaf is connected), so the leaf's tangent space is the fixed subspace n^perp and integrating the constant tangent shows the leaf lies in the affine hyperplane through any of its points with direction n^perp. Choose a flow line z(s) with z' = n; the leaf through z(s) is z(s) + z'(s)^perp. Put F(x,s)=eta(z'(s),x-z(s)) in an inertial chart and consider the smooth 5-dimensional Euclidean map H(x,s)=(x,F(x,s)). Its derivative is block triangular with upper block the4-by-4 identity and lower s-coefficient N=1+eta(z''(s),x-z(s)); at a center event x=z(s), N=1. The explicit inverse of the derivative sends (v,r) to (v,(r-D_xF(v))/N), so the choice-free smooth Euclidean inverse lemma [[lem-choice-free-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-in-euclidean-space]] gives a local smooth inverse. Because H preserves the first four coordinates, evaluating that inverse at (x,0) gives (x,sigma(x)). Shrink to product neighbourhoods where this inverse and N>0 hold; local injectivity gives unique sigma and the same hyperplane labels. This uses the ZF Euclidean supplier, not the AC-assuming Banach implicit theorem; implicit differentiation gives d sigma(v)=-eta(z'(sigma),v)/N and therefore n(sigma)=1/N; the field derivative is nabla n=d sigma (x) z''(sigma), and its acceleration is nabla_n n=z''(sigma)/N, not z''(sigma) away from the centre curve. These same formulas verify the converse: sigma-level sets are affine hyperplanes, n is constant along each leaf, so theta=omega=0. The positivity of N fixes the future-oriented tubular label. No choice principle is used; all objects are finite-dimensional and the cited ODE/flow suppliers are those of the published mathematics library.

before.title: Adopted ideal plane-wave and frequency-reading model
before.statement: Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework, extending post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light (ideal vacuum light rays are exactly the future null straight lines, with coordinate speed c in every inertial chart) and post-sr-inertial-covariance (the affine Minkowski model, with the model's equations covariant under proper orthochronous affine Lorentz maps): (i) Ideal plane wave. An ideal monochromatic light wave in vacuum is modeled, in any inertial chart, by a dimensionless affine phase theta with future null wave covector k (def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector, lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data): the level sets of theta are the wave fronts, every line p + R k^sharp has constant phase, and the rays of this ideal wave are the future null straight lines p + R_{>=0} k^sharp, consistently with the general ideal-light clause that the ideal vacuum light rays are exactly the future null straight lines. The model is one ideal plane wave: constant wave covector, no medium, no dispersion, no absorption, no modulation or envelope, no boundary or source model, no intensity or polarization model. (ii) Frequency reading. An ideal observer of the model with four-velocity U_o = c n (n future unit timelike) that receives this wave reads the angular frequency omega_n := -c k(n) = -k(U_o) and the linear frequency omega_n/(2 pi) of def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency, i.e. minus the rate of change of the phase with respect to the observer's own proper time with the sign convention that this number is positive (lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline, lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative). The reading is attached to the observer's worldline at the event of reception. (iii) Frequency comparisons. Comparing the frequency of one wave between two ideal observers or between two inertial descriptions means comparing omega_n at specified reception events, or the frame data (omega,s) of the same phase function in specified inertial charts; this postulate asserts no Doppler or aberration formula, and comparing events requires propagating the phase along the specified observer worldlines. (iv) Scope and exclusions. These are adopted idealizations, not deductions from experiment and not claims about nature. No quantum photon model and no identification of energy with hbar omega is made (excluded by the conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions); no claim is made that real light, real clocks, real receivers or real sources are exactly described; dispersive, absorbing, nonlinear or modulated media, finite line width, intensity, polarization, source and detector physics, gravitation, quantum effects and accelerated-observer reception are outside the model. Empirical tests of the model belong to the framework's experimental work and are not asserted here.
before.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it fixes the physical interpretation of the mathematical phase functions and of the observer-frequency number, and it fixes the ideal wave and receiver regime. Obligations: (i) the phase functions with future null wave covectors and their level sets are mathematical objects supplied by def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector and lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data; the identification of the level sets with wave fronts and of the future null lines along k^sharp with this wave's rays is adopted, extending the ideal-light clause of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light; for a single plane wave every future null straight line of constant phase is exactly a line p + R_{>=0} k^sharp, so the adoption introduces no competing ray system. (ii) The reading rule is an identification of a physical clock reading of a periodic process with the mathematical number -k(U_o); the mathematical positivity and the proper-time derivative are lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline and lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative, while the identification itself is adopted. (iii) The postulate is deliberately silent about Doppler and aberration formulas, so it cannot be used to infer them; the comparison protocol is fixed so that downstream theorems state exactly which frequencies at which events they compare. (iv) The exclusions are part of the adopted content and must travel with every conclusion. No proof is manufactured; no choice principle is used.

before.title: Four-momentum components, energy-velocity relation and passive boost transformation in an inertial frame
before.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with stationary observer $n:=e_0$; let $E_n,q_n$ be as in [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]].
(a) For every $P\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ the coordinate components of $P$ in the frame are $(P^0,P^1,P^2,P^3)=(E_n(P)/c,\,q^1,q^2,q^3)$, where $q_n(P)=\sum_{i=1}^3q^ie_i$; if $P$ is future timelike then $E^2=m(P)^2c^4+c^2\sum_{i=1}^3(q^i)^2$ with $E=E_n(P)$.
(b) Let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^1$ future timelike worldline whose chart coordinate path is $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$, with coordinate velocity $w:=r'$ and $\gamma_w:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$; then $|w|<c$, the four-velocity is $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$ by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e), and for $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant the components are $P=m\gamma_w(c,w)$, that is $E_n(P)=m\gamma_wc^2$ and $q_n(P)=\sum_{i=1}^3m\gamma_ww^ie_i$.
(c) Let $B(\beta)$ be the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] with parameter $\beta=v/c$, $|v|<c$, along a spatial direction $s$, and let $P'$ denote the components of the same vector $P$ after the coordinate change $x'=B(\beta)x$; write $\mathbf p=(P^1,P^2,P^3)$ and split it into its components $\mathbf p_\parallel$, $\mathbf p_\perp$ with respect to $s$. Then
$$P'^0=\gamma_v\bigl(P^0-\beta\,s\cdot\mathbf p\bigr),\qquad \mathbf p'_\parallel=\gamma_v\bigl(\mathbf p_\parallel-\beta P^0\bigr),\qquad \mathbf p'_\perp=\mathbf p_\perp,$$
equivalently $E'=\gamma_v(E-v\,p_\parallel)$, $p'_\parallel=\gamma_v(p_\parallel-vE/c^2)$, $p'_\perp=p_\perp$. The quadratic combination is invariant, $E'^2-c^2|\mathbf p'|^2=E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2=m(P)^2c^4$ for future timelike $P$, while for future null $P$ one has $E=c|\mathbf p|$ and $E'=c|\mathbf p'|$ in both coordinate systems; in particular the invariant mass is frame-independent.
before.strategy: (a) The decomposition $P=(E_n/c)e_0+q_n(P)$ of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] is already a decomposition in the basis; read components and substitute the mass-shell identity of [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(ii). (b) [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e) gives $|w|<c$ and $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$; multiply by $m$ and apply (a). (c) $P$ is a vector; the component law $v'^a=L^a{}_bv^b$ under the coordinate change $x'=Lx+b$ is [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]], and the matrix of $B(\beta)$ in the frame basis is displayed in [[def-lorentz-boost]] ($B^0{}_0=\gamma_v$, $B^0{}_i=B^i{}_0=-\gamma_v\beta s_i$, $B^i{}_j=\delta^i_j+(\gamma_v-1)s_is_j$); reading off the rows gives the displayed components, and [[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]] shows the transformed frame is inertial. The invariance is the rearrangement $E'^2-c^2|\mathbf p'|^2=E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2$ of the same components, equal to $-c^2\eta(P,P)=m(P)^2c^4$ for future timelike $P$ and to $0$ for future null $P$ ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)). No choice principle is used.

after.title: Four-momentum components, energy-velocity relation and passive boost transformation in an inertial frame
after.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with stationary observer $n:=e_0$; let $E_n,q_n$ be as in [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]].
(a) For every $P\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ the coordinate components of $P$ in the frame are $(P^0,P^1,P^2,P^3)=(E_n(P)/c,\,q^1,q^2,q^3)$, where $q_n(P)=\sum_{i=1}^3q^ie_i$; if $P$ is future timelike then $E^2=m(P)^2c^4+c^2\sum_{i=1}^3(q^i)^2$ with $E=E_n(P)$.
(b) Let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^1$ future timelike worldline whose chart coordinate path is $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$, with coordinate velocity $w:=r'$ and $\gamma_w:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$; then $|w|<c$, the four-velocity is $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$ by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e), and for $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant the components are $P=m\gamma_w(c,w)$, that is $E_n(P)=m\gamma_wc^2$ and $q_n(P)=\sum_{i=1}^3m\gamma_ww^ie_i$.
(c) Fix a unit spatial direction $s$, a signed scalar velocity $v$ with $|v|<c$, and $b:=v/c\in(-1,1)$. The passive vector boost parameter is $\boldsymbol\beta:=b s\in\mathbb R^3$, distinct from the scalar $b$. Let $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ be the boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]], let $\Lambda_b$ be its matrix in the ordered frame, and let $P'$ be the coordinate components of the same vector after $x'=\Lambda_b x$. Put $\mathbf p=(P^1,P^2,P^3)$, $p_s=s\cdot\mathbf p$, $\mathbf p_\parallel=p_s s$, $\mathbf p_\perp=\mathbf p-p_s s$, and $\gamma_v=(1-b^2)^{-1/2}$. Then
$$P'^0=\gamma_v(P^0-b p_s),\quad p'_s=\gamma_v(p_s-bP^0),\quad\mathbf p'_\parallel=\gamma_v(\mathbf p_\parallel-bP^0s),\quad\mathbf p'_\perp=\mathbf p_\perp,$$
equivalently $E'=\gamma_v(E-vp_s)$, $p'_s=\gamma_v(p_s-vE/c^2)$ and $\mathbf p'_\perp=\mathbf p_\perp$. At $b=0$ these formulas give $P'=P$, with any chosen unit $s$; no division by $b$ or choice of a boost axis from a zero vector is used. The quadratic combination is invariant, $E'^2-c^2|\mathbf p'|^2=E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2=m(P)^2c^4$ for future timelike $P$, while for future null $P$ one has $E=c|\mathbf p|$ and $E'=c|\mathbf p'|$ in both coordinate systems; in particular the invariant mass is frame-independent.
after.strategy: (a) The decomposition $P=(E_n/c)e_0+q_n(P)$ of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] is already a decomposition in the basis; read components and substitute the mass-shell identity of [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(ii). (b) [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e) gives $|w|<c$ and $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$; multiply by $m$ and apply (a). (c) The vector component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] applies to $x'=\Lambda_b x$, where $\Lambda_b$ is the displayed frame matrix of $B(bs)$. Its time row gives $P'^0=\gamma_v(P^0-bp_s)$, while its spatial block is $I+(\gamma_v-1)ss^T$ and time column $-\gamma_v b s$ for $b\ne0$. Hence $\mathbf p'=\mathbf p_\perp+\gamma_v(p_s-bP^0)s$, which yields all scalar and vector projections without a scalar-vector subtraction. For $b=0$ use $B(0)=I$, so the same projected formulas are identities for arbitrary fixed unit $s$. Proper orthochrony is [[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]. before.title: Adopted momentum model for an ideal massless particle
before.statement: Adopt as a separate model premise for ideal massless particles, independent of [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] whose formula $P=mU$ uses $m>0$ and does not define a massless case: (i) An ideal massless particle is described by a nonzero future null vector $P$ in $V$, with the SI unit kilogram metre per second of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]; it is not of the form $mU$ for any $m>0$ and any future timelike $U$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and it has no four-velocity, no proper-time parametrisation and no rest frame. Its scale is fixed by a measured energy in an observer's frame. (ii) Relative to a future unit observer $n$, the model identifies the measured energy and spatial momentum of the particle with $E_n(P)$ and $q_n(P)$ of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; necessarily $E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$ by [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a), and no rest mass, rest energy or kinetic energy is assigned. (iii) The ideal massless particle is not identified here with light, with a classical wave or with any quantum object: no frequency, wavelength, quantisation, polarisation or $\hbar$ enters, and the identification of light with massless particles requires the wave model and its own postulates on a separate page. (iv) This premise asserts no interaction of massless particles and no decay or production process; such processes require a stipulated dynamics.
before.strategy: Postulate for the massless case, kept separate because $P=mU$ at $m=0$ degenerates to $0$ ([[def-sr-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]: the zero vector is neither timelike, null nor spacelike) and cannot describe a nonzero null momentum. Obligations: (i) the object is a nonzero future null vector, using the causal classification and time orientation; (ii) the identification of $E_n$ and $q_n$ is a formulation convention, with the mathematical identity $E_n=c|q_n|$ supplied separately by [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]] and not adopted; (iii) no identification with light or with quantum concepts is made; (iv) no process is asserted. Empirical support is a nonlogical relation, not a proof.
before.physical_scope: Ideal classical massless point particles in flat Minkowski spacetime, modelled by a nonzero future null four-momentum whose energy is fixed by observation, with the model identification of measured energy and momentum. Excludes four-velocities, proper time and rest frames, any massive limit m -> 0, the identification with light or classical waves, quantum properties, and every interaction, decay, production or empirical claim.
