before.title: Distributional Maxwell equations with point and stationary-sheet sources
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the surface-measure interface inherited from [[def-em-surface-distribution]] ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units and constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $\mathcal D'(U)$ be the space of distributions on $U$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]); recall that the pairing $\langle T,\psi\rangle$ is bilinear with no conjugation and that the distributional partial derivatives are $\langle\partial_\mu T,\psi\rangle=-\langle T,\partial_\mu\psi\rangle$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]]).

(a) [Fields as distributions] Locally integrable fields and source densities on $U$ are identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]).

(b) [Point sources] Let $I_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $z:I_0\to\mathbb R^3$ be a $C^1$ trajectory whose graph map $\gamma(t)=(z(t),t)$ is proper into the open set $U$, and let $q\in\mathbb R$ (coulombs). By [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]],
$$\langle\rho_{\mathrm{pt}},\psi\rangle:=q\int_{I_0}\psi(z(t),t)\,dt,\qquad \langle J_{\mathrm{pt}},\psi\rangle:=q\int_{I_0}z'(t)\,\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$$
define distributions on $U$ with $\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{pt}}+\operatorname{div}J_{\mathrm{pt}}=0$. If instead $I_0=(a,b)$ has finite endpoints, $z$ extends continuously to $[a,b]$, the absolute improper integral $\int_a^b|z'(t)|\,dt$ is finite and both endpoint events lie in $U$, the same formulas define distributions with
$$\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{pt}}+\operatorname{div}J_{\mathrm{pt}}=q\,\delta_{\gamma(a)}-q\,\delta_{\gamma(b)}$$
([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]); a finite-history point source therefore contributes an endpoint term unless that term is included explicitly, and the pairings above exclude it only by the stated properness or endpoint hypotheses.

(c) [Stationary-sheet sources] Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]], [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]), and let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current density; the sheet is stationary). Then
$$\langle\rho_S,\psi\rangle:=\int_I\int_S\sigma(x,t)\psi(x,t)\,dS(x)\,dt,\qquad \langle J_S,\psi\rangle:=\int_I\int_SK(x,t)\psi(x,t)\,dS(x)\,dt$$
define distributions on $U$: for $\psi$ with compact support the inner integrals are continuous in $t$ on a compact parameter interval and the functionals are bounded by $(\sup|\sigma\psi|)\,\mathrm{area}(S)\,\mathrm{length}$ of the time projection of the support, and likewise in the vector case. A normal sheet current (one with $K\cdot n\ne0$), a line current and a moving sheet are not source types of this definition.

(d) [Unrestricted weak fields and optional interface branches] The general field class for the solution predicate (e) consists of all locally integrable pairs $(E,B)$ on $U$, also when the source has a stationary-sheet part. No classical one-sided trace or off-sheet $C^1$ regularity is required to define those four distributional pairings. Additional trace hypotheses are optional hypotheses of interface/jump results, not admission requirements of the general weak model.
For a pointwise classical jump branch, one may additionally assume that $E,B$ are $C^1$ off $S\times I$ and, around every $(x_0,t_0)\in S\times I$, each side is the restriction of a $C^1$ function on an open spacetime neighborhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller stationary graph cylinder. These joint one-sided extensions make the field traces and first spatial/temporal derivatives continuous up to that side, locally uniformly on compact cylinders.
For the broader weak-trace branch, one may instead assume the original one-sided spatial $C^1$ extensions at each time, with the explicit additional conditions that the piecewise first spatial and temporal derivatives are in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(U)$ and the field traces are measurable and locally integrable on $S\times I$ for $dSdt$. This branch supports sheet-distribution and almost-everywhere jump identities; spatial continuity at each time gives pointwise spatial identities for almost every time, and joint continuity of the jump densities gives the further all-time upgrade. Separate spatial $C^1$ traces at each time alone do not imply that joint regularity or upgrade. Whenever such traces exist, $[F]:=F_+-F_-$ denotes their jump in the chosen normal convention. (e) [Weak Maxwell equations with a distributional source pair] Let $E,B$ be a field pair of class (d), let $\rho=\rho_v+\rho_s$ and $J=J_v+J_s$ be source distributions on $U$ whose volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are locally integrable volume densities with the charge/current quantity types of [[def-em-sources]] (the weak predicate requires this stated $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity, not the classical continuous-source regularity) and whose singular parts $(\rho_s,J_s)$ are point sources as in (b) or stationary-sheet sources as in (c), and let $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Say that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair $(\rho,J)$ when, for every $\psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$, the four pairings
$$\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$$
all vanish, all derivatives being distributional derivatives of the regular distributions of the fields and the source pairings being those of (b) and (c). This clause defines a solution predicate. When the singular parts vanish, its four identities are the same as the locally integrable weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. That earlier postulate explicitly excludes point and sheet distributions and does not imply their physical adoption here; adoption for the declared singular-source models is made separately, after this definition. No physical field equation is deduced merely from defining this predicate.

(f) [Scope] No product of two distributions is formed anywhere: the fields occur only through their distributional derivatives paired with a test function, and the source densities $\sigma,K$ occur only inside the ordinary surface and time integrals of (b) and (c); products such as $\rho_sE$ or $J_s\times B$ are not defined by this item. The definition asserts no existence theorem for fields with singular sources, no conservation law (continuity for these sources is proved separately where used), and no regularisation. Sources that are not locally integrable and are not point or stationary-sheet sources, moving sheets, line currents, and arbitrary products of distributions are outside the definition.
before.strategy: An explicit definition-contract item. Clause (a) is the regular-distribution identification. Clause (b) restates the pairings and the continuity theorem of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] with its properness hypothesis, and its finite-endpoint variant with the two endpoint deltas. Clause (c) defines the stationary-sheet pairings by explicit iterated integrals; well-definedness uses the finiteness of the surface measure of the compact $S$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[def-em-surface-distribution]]), continuity of $\sigma,K,\psi$ on compact sets and compactness of the time projection of the support of a test function, so both functionals are continuous of finite order on each test-support space. Clause (d) retains the unrestricted locally integrable field pair for the weak predicate, including sheet sources. It records optional interface hypotheses separately: joint one-sided spacetime C1 extensions support the pointwise branch; the weaker per-time spatial C1 trace branch needs the explicit piecewise-derivative and sheet-trace L1 hypotheses for its distribution/a.e. conclusions. Neither branch is a general weak-field admission condition, and separate spatial C1 traces alone are not claimed to give joint continuity or temporal bounds. Clause (e) defines the weak equations by the four vanishing pairings, with distributional derivatives of the regular distributions of the fields; the singular source terms enter only as the explicitly defined functionals of (b) and (c), never as products with the fields. Clause (f) records the exclusions; in particular the product of a singular source density with a field, which would be an undefined product of distributions, is not part of the definition. The vanishing-pairing clause is a precise mathematical solution predicate. It agrees with the old postulate on its original locally integrable source class, but does not extend that physical postulate deductively to singular sources; physical adoption is a separate postulate. It remains possible for a declared source pair to be incompatible with those equations, and no existence is asserted.

before.title: Adopted massive-particle momentum, observer measurement and isolated-collision conservation
before.statement: Adopt as physical assumptions of the relativistic particle model, on top of the flat spacetime model, the ideal-clock and ideal-light postulates and the SI unit conventions: (i) Mass and momentum. Every massive classical particle carries a positive constant invariant mass parameter $m>0$ and has four-momentum $P=mU$, where $U$ is the four-velocity of its future timelike worldline; $P$ is a vector of $V$ whose SI unit is kilogram metre per second. The formula is adopted only for $m>0$; the case $m=0$ is not defined by it and is a separate premise. (ii) Observer measurement identification. Relative to a future unit observer $n$, the model identifies the measured energy of the particle with $E_n(P)$, its measured spatial momentum with $q_n(P)$, its kinetic energy with $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ and its rest energy with $mc^2$, where $E_n,q_n,T_n$ are the quantities of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; the units are the joule, kilogram metre per second and kilogram of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. This clause is a formulation convention identifying mathematical quantities with the quantities the model calls measured; it is not a measurement report and no experiment is claimed. (iii) Isolated collision balance. In an isolated collision of particles at an event -- the interaction being confined to that event, with no external agent acting -- the sum of the incoming four-momenta equals the sum of the outgoing four-momenta, in the sense of [[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]]. No particular collision is asserted to occur, and no mechanism, probability, cross section or amplitude is supplied by this clause. (iv) Equation of motion. Whenever an interaction is described by a stipulated force, the model's particle equation is $m\,dU/d\tau=F(x,U)$ with $F$ the four-force of [[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]]; a particular force law (the dependence of $F$ on position and four-velocity) and the existence, uniqueness or domain of solutions are not adopted here and belong to a separate model.
before.strategy: Postulate: an adopted physical premise, not a theorem. Obligations: (i) $P=mU$ uses the four-velocity of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-acceleration]] with its normalisation $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]; (ii) the measurement identification names the mathematical quantities $E_n,q_n,T_n$ of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] and the SI units of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and explicitly disclaims observation; (iii) conservation is stated for an isolated collision only, as an equality of the side totals of [[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]], with no existence or mechanism claim; (iv) the equation of motion form is adopted only for a stipulated force, and no force law is adopted. Empirical support for the assumptions is a nonlogical relation of the framework, not a proof; the idealisations of point particles, ideal clocks and flat spacetime are inherited and must travel to consumers.
before.physical_scope: Classical massive point particles with positive constant invariant mass in flat Minkowski spacetime, with ideal clocks and ideal light and the SI conventions: the model identifies the observer quantities E_n, q_n, T_n as the measured energy, momentum and kinetic energy, and adopts exact four-momentum conservation for isolated collisions at one event. Excludes massless particles, internal structure, spin, radiation reaction, variable mass, gravity, continuum matter, quantum and statistical effects, and every empirical or measurement claim; a force law and any interaction mechanism are separate premises.

before.title: The uniformly accelerated worldline: hyperbolic motion, constant four-acceleration magnitude, and identification as a Rindler flow line
before.statement: Let c > 0 and alpha > 0, set R := c^2/alpha, and let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space with an inertial chart x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3), x^0 = c t (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model, def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Let x: R -> A be the curve x(tau) := x^{-1}(R sinh theta, R cosh theta, 0, 0), where theta := alpha tau/c. (a) Regularity, causal character and parametrization. x is C^infinity, and x'(tau) = c(cosh theta, sinh theta, 0, 0) is future timelike for every tau (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets), so x is a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline). Since eta(x',x') = -c^2 is constant, the parameter tau is a proper-time parameter of the curve: the proper-time function tau of def-sr-proper-time satisfies tau(b) - tau(a) = b - a for all a < b in R (def-sr-proper-time, lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization), and the four-velocity is U := dx/dtau = c(cosh theta, sinh theta, 0, 0) with eta(U,U) = -c^2 (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a)). (b) Constant four-acceleration magnitude. The four-acceleration A := dU/dtau = alpha(sinh theta, cosh theta, 0, 0) satisfies eta(A,A) = alpha^2 and eta(U,A) = 0. The chart coordinate velocity is dx^1/dt = c tanh theta, so |dx^1/dt| < c for every tau, and x^1 = R cosh theta > R|sinh theta| = |x^0| for every tau: the worldline lies in the right wedge W := {x^1 > |x^0|} and its speed in the chart tends to c only as tau -> +-infinity. (c) Rindler flow line. Let Phi(theta,rho,y,z) := (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) on R x (0,inf) x R^2 and let n := rho^{-1} partial_theta be the Rindler congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b), whose pullback metric is -rho^2 dtheta^2 + drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 and whose congruence acceleration a_cg := nabla_n n is rho^{-1} partial_rho, with eta(a_cg,a_cg) = rho^{-2} (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space, def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics). Then x is exactly the flow line Phi(., R, 0, 0) reparametrized by theta = alpha tau/c, and along x one has A = c^2 a_cg: the four-acceleration of the worldline is c^2 times the congruence acceleration, and eta(a_cg,a_cg) = 1/R^2 = alpha^2/c^4 on the flow line rho = R. (d) Asymptotic behaviour. Along x one has x^1 - x^0 = R e^{-theta} -> 0 with x^0 -> +infinity as tau -> +infinity, and x^1 + x^0 = R e^{theta} -> 0 with x^0 -> -infinity as tau -> -infinity: the worldline approaches each of the null planes {x^1 = x^0} and {x^1 = -x^0} asymptotically without meeting either, and the chart coordinate speed tends to c at both ends. (e) Scope. This is an exact kinematic computation in the affine model. It uses no force law, no mass, no clock hypothesis and no empirical input; beyond identifying the displayed parameter with the proper time of the curve, only the flow parametrization of the congruence is used. The curve is not asserted to be a geodesic and no statement is made about the forces that would maintain it. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Exact computation with the hyperbolic identities and their derivatives. (a) Differentiating the two components of x with the chain rule (thm-chain-rule, def-derivative) and thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives gives x' = c(cosh theta, sinh theta, 0, 0); cosh > 0 makes it future and eta(x',x') = c^2(-cosh^2 + sinh^2) = -c^2 (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). The integrand of def-sr-proper-time is the constant c, so its integral over [a,b] is c(b-a) and tau(b) - tau(a) = b - a; the assertions about the four-velocity then follow from lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization (iv) and thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a). (b) Differentiating U gives A = alpha(sinh theta, cosh theta, 0, 0); eta(A,A) = alpha^2(cosh^2 - sinh^2) = alpha^2 and eta(U,A) = c alpha(-cosh sinh + sinh cosh) = 0 (thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives); the chart velocity is dx^1/dt = (dx^1/dtau)/(dt/dtau) = c sinh/cosh = c tanh, and cosh > |sinh| gives the wedge and the speed bound. (c) Direct comparison: Phi(theta, R, 0, 0) = (R sinh theta, R cosh theta, 0, 0) = x(tau) with theta = alpha tau/c, and the congruence data are those of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b); the identity A = c^2 a_cg is proved directly on the flow line: since dx/dtau = c n there, d(n o x)/dtau = nabla_{dx/dtau} n = c nabla_n n = c a_cg by the defining properties of the flat covariant derivative along curves (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (d)), so A = dU/dtau = c d(n o x)/dtau = c^2 a_cg. (d) The identities x^1 -+ x^0 = R(cosh -+ sinh) = R e^{-+theta} and e^{+-theta} -> 0 (thm-exponential-limits-and-range) give the limits; tanh -> +-1 gives the speed statement. (e) Scope only. No choice principle is used: all steps are finite-dimensional algebra and calculus.

before.title: The static and pure electrostatic regimes and their fixed-time reading
before.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units, constants and symbols of [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ and $B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be fields of [[def-em-fields]] and let $(\rho,J)$ be source fields of [[def-em-sources]] on $\Omega\times I$, all of class $C^1$ (with every additional derivative appearing below existing and continuous); $\partial_t$ is the partial time derivative at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].
(a) [Static regime] The **static (time-independent) electromagnetic regime** on $\Omega\times I$ is the requirement
$$\partial_tE=0,\qquad\partial_tB=0,\qquad\partial_t\rho=0,\qquad\partial_tJ=0\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$
(b) [Pure electrostatics] The **pure electrostatic regime** is the static regime together with $J=0$ and $B=0$ on $\Omega\times I$.
(c) [Reduced equations] If the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds in the static regime, then the four Maxwell equations reduce to
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}E=0,\qquad\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$$
pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, with $\operatorname{div}$ and $\operatorname{curl}$ of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] applied at each fixed time; in the pure electrostatic regime the reduction is exactly the pair $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0$.
(d) [Fixed-time reading] In the static regime $E,B,\rho,J$ do not depend on $t$, so each is the pullback along $(y,t)\mapsto y$ of a single map on $\Omega$; this fixed-time reading (the spatial field or source) is the object analysed by the electrostatic statements of this page, and no other time dependence is introduced. The equations of (c) are equations between those spatial maps.
(e) [Static-to-distributional reading] Let fields $E,B$ and volume densities $\rho,J$ be locally integrable and time independent on $\Omega\times I$, and let $\Omega$ be open. Then, under the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of the cited measure and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]), the weak equations of the solution predicate of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e) for these time-independent objects hold if and only if the four spatial equations $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0$, $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ hold in $\mathcal D'(\Omega)$; the passage between them is the integration in $t$ of the pairings against $C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$ tests, justified by [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] after identifying fields and densities with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). In particular a **stationary point charge** at $x_0\in\Omega$ with charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ is the point source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) with constant trajectory $z(t)\equiv x_0$, whose pairing is $\psi\mapsto q\int_I\psi(x_0,t)\,dt$ and whose fixed-time reading is the spatial point source $\eta\mapsto q\eta(x_0)$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]).
(f) [Conventions and scope] The regime is imposed in the one inertial frame of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]; no claim is made that time independence survives a change of inertial description, and where a frame change is used the transformed fields must be rechecked. The static regime is an adopted idealization, not a dynamical stability theorem: static charged matter requires external support or an adopted equilibrium model. No equation is asserted here for singular sources beyond the dictionary of (e), and no empirical claim is made.
before.strategy: For the locally integrable branch use Borel representatives of each spatial component, obtained under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from [[cor-lebesgue-sigma-algebra-is-the-completion-of-borel-lebesgue-measure]] and [[thm-completion-measurable-functions-have-base-measurable-representatives]] after zero extension outside $\Omega$. These changes are on spatial null sets and their products with compact time intervals are null, so they do not change spatial or spacetime regular distributions. With [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]] and [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]], the pairings may therefore be evaluated using the product measure and Fubini below. Conversely, testing with $\psi(y,t)=\eta(y)\chi(t)$ for $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, $\chi\in C_c^\infty(I)$ with $\int\chi=1$ recovers the spatial equations, using that all objects are time independent. Clause (f) records the frame dependence and the idealization; no boost statement and no dynamics are asserted, so nothing beyond the cited definitions and the two integrations is used. Finite-interval integrations of the continuous one-variable test/radial integrands above use [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] to identify their Riemann/FTC values with their Lebesgue values before Fubini, polar integration or passage to improper limits; real and imaginary test components are treated separately.

after.title: The static and pure electrostatic regimes and their fixed-time reading

(a) [Static regime] The **static (time-independent) electromagnetic regime** on $\Omega\times I$ is the requirement
$$\partial_tE=0,\qquad\partial_tB=0,\qquad\partial_t\rho=0,\qquad\partial_tJ=0\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$
(b) [Pure electrostatics] The **pure electrostatic regime** is the static regime together with $J=0$ and $B=0$ on $\Omega\times I$.
(c) [Reduced equations] If the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds in the static regime, then the four Maxwell equations reduce to
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}E=0,\qquad\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$$
pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, with $\operatorname{div}$ and $\operatorname{curl}$ of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] applied at each fixed time; in the pure electrostatic regime the reduction is exactly the pair $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0$.
(d) [Fixed-time reading] In the static regime $E,B,\rho,J$ do not depend on $t$, so each is the pullback along $(y,t)\mapsto y$ of a single map on $\Omega$; this fixed-time reading (the spatial field or source) is the object analysed by the electrostatic statements of this page, and no other time dependence is introduced. before.title: Stationary-sheet jump conditions of the weak Maxwell equations
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the interface and surface-measure definitions cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and source fields of [[def-em-sources]].

Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]]), and let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current density). Let $E,B$ be locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$ and $C^1$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ with the following explicit joint one-sided regularity: around every $(x_0,t_0)\in S\times I$, each side is the restriction of a $C^1$ function on an open spacetime neighbourhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller stationary graph cylinder. Thus the fields and their first space/time derivatives extend continuously to that side of $S\times I$, locally uniformly on compact cylinders, and let $\rho_v,J_v$ be continuous on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ and locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$. Write $[F]=F_+-F_-$ for the jump of the one-sided traces of such a field $F$.

Under the separate singular-source physical adoption [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], suppose that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair
$$\rho=\rho_v+\rho_S,\qquad J=J_v+J_S,$$
where $(\rho_S,J_S)$ is the stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) with densities $\sigma,K$ and the pairings there, in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e), and where the volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Then, pointwise on $S\times I$,
$$n\cdot[E]=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad n\times[B]=\mu_0K,\qquad n\cdot[B]=0,\qquad n\times[E]=0,$$
with the ordinary Euclidean inner and cross products of the one-sided traces ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Equivalently, the surface current density is $K=(\mu_0)^{-1}\,n\times[B]$ and the surface charge density is $\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot[E]$.

The theorem assumes a stationary interface: the hypersurface $S$ and its normal do not depend on $t$, so the one-sided $C^1$ traces also make $\partial_tE$ and $\partial_tB$ locally bounded near $S$ and hence locally integrable, contributing no delta terms. No magnetic surface charge or magnetic surface current is present in the sources, and correspondingly the last two identities assert the absence of magnetic sheet delta terms. A moving interface, a normal sheet current, or a sheet whose support changes with time is outside this statement and would require additional terms.

[General weak trace branch] The weak Maxwell framework continues to allow the full locally integrable field/source class, without asserting undefined classical trace values. If instead of the joint extension condition the fields have the original one-sided spatial $C^1$ extensions at each time, assume in addition that their piecewise first spatial and temporal derivatives are in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega\times I)$ and that their one-sided field traces are measurable and locally integrable on $S\times I$ with respect to $dS\,dt$. Then the same four jump identities hold as equalities of sheet distributions and for $dS\,dt$-almost every $(x,t)$; since the traces are spatially continuous at each fixed time, they hold for every $x\in S$ for almost every $t\in I$. They hold at every $(x,t)$ whenever the jump densities are additionally jointly continuous. Merely having one-sided spatial $C^1$ traces separately at every time does not justify this last upgrade.
before.strategy:
First justify the spacetime use of the spatial supplier. For a compactly supported spacetime test $\psi$, let $K\subset\Omega$ be its compact spatial support projection and let $L\Subset I$ be a compact interval containing its time support. Choose finitely many spatial stationary graph neighbourhoods and interior open sets covering $K$. [[lem-finite-ambient-partitions-for-euclidean-boundary-integration]] gives smooth nonnegative spatial functions $\phi_j$ compactly supported in those sets with $\sum_j\phi_j=1$ near $K$. Explicitly, first choose finitely many nonnegative ambient bumps $\chi_j$ subordinate to that cover whose sum $s$ is positive near $K$; a cutoff $\theta\in C_c^\infty(\{s>0\})$ equal to one near $K$ exists by [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]], and $\phi_j=\theta\chi_j/s$ on $\{s>0\}$, extended by zero elsewhere, is smooth since $\operatorname{supp}\theta$ stays compactly inside the positive set. Their sum is $\theta=1$ near $K$, so $\psi=\sum_j\phi_j\psi$. This partition is independent of time, hence $\partial_t(\phi_j\psi)=\phi_j\partial_t\psi$ and temporal integration by parts acquires no partition derivative. On each spatial chart times $L$, the local joint one-sided extensions have a finite subcover of the relevant compact sheet-time subset, giving the compact bounds used below; interior compact supports are already covered by the ordinary joint $C^1$ assumption. In the joint branch the one-sided $C^1$ extensions and their derivatives are bounded on each compact closed half-cylinder, so the piecewise derivatives are locally integrable and the jumps are jointly continuous and bounded there. Apply [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] to each component of the spatial slice at every fixed $t$ and integrate in $t$. The terms $F\partial_i\psi$, $(\partial_i F)\psi$ and $n_i[F]\psi$ are absolutely integrable on the compact support (the last uses the finite compact surface measure of [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]), so [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] justifies integrating the identity. This gives $\partial_iF_j=\{\partial_iF_j\}+n_i[F_j]\delta_{S\times I}$, and contraction/antisymmetrization gives the divergence/curl formulas. For the temporal derivative, on each fixed spatial side, [[thm-integration-by-parts]] on a compact time interval containing the test support, followed by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], gives $-\int F_j\partial_t\psi=\int (\partial_tF_j)\psi$, with no endpoint term since the test support is compact in $I$. Integrate in $x$ by the same Fubini theorem. The sides are stationary, so no derivative of a moving spatial indicator occurs and $\partial_tF_j=\{\partial_tF_j\}$ with no sheet term.

The spatial sheet $S$ has three-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero: in each finite graph chart every normal section is a singleton, so Fubini gives zero volume, and the coordinate permutation preserves Lebesgue measure. Consequently $S\times I$ is locally four-dimensional null. Restrict each weak Maxwell identity to tests away from $S\times I$. The resulting ordinary residuals are continuous on the open complement, so the existing sign-and-ambient-bump argument forces them to vanish pointwise there. The ordinary residuals are locally integrable and differ from zero only on the null sheet, hence represent zero regular distributions by [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]]. Subtract them to obtain the four sheet identities with densities $n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n\cdot[B]$, $n\times[E]$, $n\times[B]-\mu_0K$. For every spatial $\varphi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, each scalar component $H(t)=\int_S a(x,t)\varphi(x)\,dS$ is continuous: on a compact time interval, joint continuity on the compact sheet gives uniform convergence as $t\to t_0$, and the bound $|H(t)-H(t_0)|\le S(S)\|\varphi\|_\infty\sup_{x\in S}|a(x,t)-a(x,t_0)|$ tends to zero. Testing $\varphi(x)\eta(t)$ and using the one-dimensional sign-and-bump argument shows $H(t)=0$ at every time. Apply [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]] at that time and componentwise to get the four pointwise jumps. Tangentiality of $n\times[B]$ gives the stated current formula.

For the general weak trace branch, the additional local $L^1$ hypotheses on piecewise derivatives and traces justify the same Fubini arguments without compact uniform bounds. Temporal integration by parts is valid first on compact subintervals for each fixed off-sheet $x$, since the field is $C^1$ there; its integrable derivative and the test's compact support justify the integrated identity. The sheet residuals are therefore zero as distributions. For each fixed ambient spatial test $\varphi$, Fubini gives the locally integrable time function $H_\varphi(t)=\int_S a(x,t)\varphi(x)\,dS$, and testing $\varphi(x)\eta(t)$ shows its regular distribution is zero. The one-dimensional case of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] gives $H_\varphi(t)=0$ for almost every time. To obtain one exceptional time set, use the countable explicit ambient bumps with rational centres $q\in\mathbb Q^3$ and rational radii $0<r<R$ for which $\overline B_R(q)\subset\Omega$, equal to one on $\overline B_r(q)$ and supported in $B_R(q)$. They are defined by the fixed smooth-step formula in [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], so no arbitrary choice of a test for each triple is needed. Remove the countable union of the null time sets for these tests, which remains null by [[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]]. For a remaining time, a nonzero continuous spatial residual at any $x_0\in S$ has one strict sign on a sufficiently small graph neighbourhood. Density of the rationals ([[lem-q-and-irrationals-dense-r]]) gives one of those ambient balls wholly inside that neighbourhood whose inner ball contains $x_0$. A positive-area graph cell in its inner ball, as in [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]], makes its pairing nonzero, contradiction. Thus each residual vanishes at every spatial point for almost every time, which also proves the sheet-a.e. assertion. Joint continuity, if separately assumed, similarly upgrades to all times using positive-area cells times nondegenerate time intervals. The counterexample recorded in this proposal proves why this qualification cannot be omitted. All four electromagnetic conclusions and the unrestricted weak Maxwell framework are retained at their strongest justified regularity level; no Sobolev trace theorem or undeclared Choice principle is used.

before.physical_scope: The stationary-sheet jump conditions of the classical electromagnetic framework in a named inertial laboratory frame: for locally integrable fields that are piecewise $C^1$ across a fixed compact interface, solving the weak Maxwell equations with a prescribed surface charge density $\sigma$ and tangential surface current density $K$ forces $n\cdot[E]=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n\times[B]=\mu_0K$, $n\cdot[B]=0$ and $n\times[E]=0$, with the jump taken along the chosen normal from the minus to the plus side. The statement excludes moving interfaces, normal sheet currents and magnetic sheet sources, asserts no measurement or apparatus realisation, and carries the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of the interface and surface-measure items. Pointwise classical jumps use the explicit joint one-sided regularity or an independently established jointly continuous jump; the specified locally integrable trace branch gives sheet-distribution and almost-everywhere jumps. The unrestricted L1 weak framework does not by itself define pointwise classical traces.

after.title: Stationary-sheet jump conditions of the weak Maxwell equations
after.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the interface and surface-measure definitions cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and source fields of [[def-em-sources]].

Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]]), and let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current density). Let $E,B$ be locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$ and $C^1$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ with the following explicit joint one-sided regularity: around every $(x_0,t_0)\in S\times I$, each side is the restriction of a $C^1$ function on an open spacetime neighbourhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller stationary graph cylinder. Thus the fields and their first space/time derivatives extend continuously to that side of $S\times I$, locally uniformly on compact cylinders, and let $\rho_v,J_v$ be continuous on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ and locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$. Write $[F]=F_+-F_-$ for the jump of the one-sided traces of such a field $F$.

Under the separate singular-source physical adoption [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], suppose that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair
$$\rho=\rho_v+\rho_S,\qquad J=J_v+J_S,$$
where $(\rho_S,J_S)$ is the stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) with densities $\sigma,K$ and the pairings there, in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e), and where the volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Then, pointwise on $S\times I$,
$$n\cdot[E]=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad n\times[B]=\mu_0K,\qquad n\cdot[B]=0,\qquad n\times[E]=0,$$
with the ordinary Euclidean inner and cross products of the one-sided traces ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Equivalently, the surface current density is $K=(\mu_0)^{-1}\,n\times[B]$ and the surface charge density is $\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot[E]$.

The theorem assumes a stationary interface: the hypersurface $S$ and its normal do not depend on $t$, so the one-sided $C^1$ traces also make $\partial_tE$ and $\partial_tB$ locally bounded near $S$ and hence locally integrable, contributing no delta terms. No magnetic surface charge or magnetic surface current is present in the sources, and correspondingly the last two identities assert the absence of magnetic sheet delta terms. A moving interface, a normal sheet current, or a sheet whose support changes with time is outside this statement and would require additional terms.

[General weak trace branch] The weak Maxwell framework continues to allow the full locally integrable field/source class, without asserting undefined classical trace values. If instead of the joint extension condition the fields have the original one-sided spatial $C^1$ extensions at each time, assume in addition that their piecewise first spatial and temporal derivatives are in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega\times I)$ and that their one-sided field traces are measurable and locally integrable on $S\times I$ with respect to $dS\,dt$. Then the same four jump identities hold as equalities of sheet distributions and for $dS\,dt$-almost every $(x,t)$; since the traces are spatially continuous at each fixed time, they hold for every $x\in S$ for almost every $t\in I$. They hold at every $(x,t)$ whenever the jump densities are additionally jointly continuous. Merely having one-sided spatial $C^1$ traces separately at every time does not justify this last upgrade. In this weak branch temporal derivatives in $L^1_{\rm loc}$ are genuine weak derivatives, or classical derivatives with the joint interior $C^1$ integration-by-parts justification already assumed. More generally, that temporal integrability hypothesis may be omitted when the stated spatial derivative and trace integrability and the actual fixed-sheet weak equations with regular volume sources hold: those equations themselves imply the same jumps and regular temporal derivatives. No joint boundary continuity is imposed on this broader branch.
after.strategy:
First justify the spacetime use of the spatial supplier. For a compactly supported spacetime test $\psi$, let $K\subset\Omega$ be its compact spatial support projection and let $L\Subset I$ be a compact interval containing its time support. Choose finitely many spatial stationary graph neighbourhoods and interior open sets covering $K$. [[lem-finite-ambient-partitions-for-euclidean-boundary-integration]] gives smooth nonnegative spatial functions $\phi_j$ compactly supported in those sets with $\sum_j\phi_j=1$ near $K$. Explicitly, first choose finitely many nonnegative ambient bumps $\chi_j$ subordinate to that cover whose sum $s$ is positive near $K$; a cutoff $\theta\in C_c^\infty(\{s>0\})$ equal to one near $K$ exists by [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]], and $\phi_j=\theta\chi_j/s$ on $\{s>0\}$, extended by zero elsewhere, is smooth since $\operatorname{supp}\theta$ stays compactly inside the positive set. Their sum is $\theta=1$ near $K$, so $\psi=\sum_j\phi_j\psi$. This partition is independent of time, hence $\partial_t(\phi_j\psi)=\phi_j\partial_t\psi$ and temporal integration by parts acquires no partition derivative. On each spatial chart times $L$, the local joint one-sided extensions have a finite subcover of the relevant compact sheet-time subset, giving the compact bounds used below; interior compact supports are already covered by the ordinary joint $C^1$ assumption. In the joint branch the one-sided $C^1$ extensions and their derivatives are bounded on each compact closed half-cylinder, so the piecewise derivatives are locally integrable and the jumps are jointly continuous and bounded there. Apply [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] to each component of the spatial slice at every fixed $t$ and integrate in $t$. The terms $F\partial_i\psi$, $(\partial_i F)\psi$ and $n_i[F]\psi$ are absolutely integrable on the compact support (the last uses the finite compact surface measure of [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]), so [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] justifies integrating the identity. This gives $\partial_iF_j=\{\partial_iF_j\}+n_i[F_j]\delta_{S\times I}$, and contraction/antisymmetrization gives the divergence/curl formulas. For the temporal derivative, on each fixed spatial side, [[thm-integration-by-parts]] on a compact time interval containing the test support, followed by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], gives $-\int F_j\partial_t\psi=\int (\partial_tF_j)\psi$, with no endpoint term since the test support is compact in $I$. Integrate in $x$ by the same Fubini theorem. The sides are stationary, so no derivative of a moving spatial indicator occurs and $\partial_tF_j=\{\partial_tF_j\}$ with no sheet term.

The spatial sheet $S$ has three-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero: in each finite graph chart every normal section is a singleton, so Fubini gives zero volume, and the coordinate permutation preserves Lebesgue measure. Consequently $S\times I$ is locally four-dimensional null. Restrict each weak Maxwell identity to tests away from $S\times I$. The resulting ordinary residuals are continuous on the open complement, so the existing sign-and-ambient-bump argument forces them to vanish pointwise there. The ordinary residuals are locally integrable and differ from zero only on the null sheet, hence represent zero regular distributions by [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]]. Subtract them to obtain the four sheet identities with densities $n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n\cdot[B]$, $n\times[E]$, $n\times[B]-\mu_0K$. For every spatial $\varphi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, each scalar component $H(t)=\int_S a(x,t)\varphi(x)\,dS$ is continuous: on a compact time interval, joint continuity on the compact sheet gives uniform convergence as $t\to t_0$, and the bound $|H(t)-H(t_0)|\le S(S)\|\varphi\|_\infty\sup_{x\in S}|a(x,t)-a(x,t_0)|$ tends to zero. Testing $\varphi(x)\eta(t)$ and using the one-dimensional sign-and-bump argument shows $H(t)=0$ at every time. Apply [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]] at that time and componentwise to get the four pointwise jumps. Tangentiality of $n\times[B]$ gives the stated current formula.

For the general weak trace branch, the additional local $L^1$ hypotheses on piecewise derivatives and traces justify the same Fubini arguments without compact uniform bounds. Temporal integration by parts is valid first on compact subintervals for each fixed off-sheet $x$, since the field is $C^1$ there; its integrable derivative and the test's compact support justify the integrated identity. The sheet residuals are therefore zero as distributions. For each fixed ambient spatial test $\varphi$, Fubini gives the locally integrable time function $H_\varphi(t)=\int_S a(x,t)\varphi(x)\,dS$, and testing $\varphi(x)\eta(t)$ shows its regular distribution is zero. The one-dimensional case of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] gives $H_\varphi(t)=0$ for almost every time. To obtain one exceptional time set, use the countable explicit ambient bumps with rational centres $q\in\mathbb Q^3$ and rational radii $0<r<R$ for which $\overline B_R(q)\subset\Omega$, equal to one on $\overline B_r(q)$ and supported in $B_R(q)$. They are defined by the fixed smooth-step formula in [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], so no arbitrary choice of a test for each triple is needed. Remove the countable union of the null time sets for these tests, which remains null by [[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]]. For a remaining time, a nonzero continuous spatial residual at any $x_0\in S$ has one strict sign on a sufficiently small graph neighbourhood. Density of the rationals ([[lem-q-and-irrationals-dense-r]]) gives one of those ambient balls wholly inside that neighbourhood whose inner ball contains $x_0$. A positive-area graph cell in its inner ball, as in [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]], makes its pairing nonzero, contradiction. Thus each residual vanishes at every spatial point for almost every time, which also proves the sheet-a.e. assertion. Joint continuity, if separately assumed, similarly upgrades to all times using positive-area cells times nondegenerate time intervals. The counterexample recorded in this proposal proves why this qualification cannot be omitted. All four electromagnetic conclusions and the unrestricted weak Maxwell framework are retained at their strongest justified regularity level; no Sobolev trace theorem or undeclared Choice principle is used. To justify the broader weak branch directly, first apply the regular-L1 specialization of the spatial interface lemma at each admissible time and integrate by Fubini. Its spatial distributional sheet coefficient is the stated trace jump. Work on a compact graph patch with a smooth tube cutoff chi_epsilon(y), independent of time, equal to one on the sheet, bounded between zero and one, and supported where |z-g(y)|<2epsilon; multiply by a fixed compact test. This cutoff need only be C2 for a C2 graph: all equations involved are order at most one. To use it legitimately, approximate the resulting compactly supported C1 test in the C1 norm by smooth tests via [[thm-convolution-with-a-mollifier-is-smooth-and-differentiates-under-the-integral-sign]], using its actual kernel-footprint margin. For each derivative of order at most one, move the derivative to the compact C1 input by classical integration by parts and write the error as integral eta(v)[D^alpha f(x-epsilon v)-D^alpha f(x)]dv. Uniform continuity on one compact enlarged support and the finite integral of |eta| make this error uniformly vanish; no unit-support assumption is made. The L1 and finite sheet measures make all pairings continuous in that norm, so the weak identities extend to it. For a temporal term its absolute pairing is at most the integral over the shrinking spatial tube of |F| times the fixed time-derivative bound. For a regular spatial bulk or volume source use its absolute L1 majorant. The sheet has ambient volume zero, and [[thm-dominated-convergence]] sends all these integrals to zero. The sheet term survives unchanged because chi_epsilon=1 on S. Thus the four weak equations force exactly their four displayed sheet coefficients, without assuming a temporal classical derivative is integrable or demanding joint continuous boundary values. After cancelling these coefficients, the curl evolution equations identify the weak temporal derivatives with their regular spatial bulk and volume-source expressions, which are L1loc. The existing scalar-test localization and Countable Choice a.e.-time argument then give the stated sheet-a.e., spatial-continuity and joint-continuity upgrades. The original jointly C1 interior branch is included and supports its classical temporal integration by parts; the general given-L1 Maxwell admission stays unrestricted.

before.title: Stationary macroscopic interface jump conditions for D, B, E and H
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis under which [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] and the surface conventions of [[def-em-weak-sources]] are stated, and let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]].
Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]]), let $\sigma_f:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K_f:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K_f(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a free surface charge density and a tangential free surface current density, both stationary in $t$), and let $\rho_v:(\Omega\setminus S)\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $J_v:(\Omega\setminus S)\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous and locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$. Let $E,B,D,H:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$ and of class $C^1$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$, with the joint one-sided $C^1$ extension property: around every $(x_0,t_0)\in S\times I$, each side of each field is the restriction of a $C^1$ function on an open spacetime neighbourhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller stationary graph cylinder, so that the fields and their first space and time derivatives extend continuously to that side, locally uniformly on compact cylinders. Write $[F]=F_+-F_-$ for the jump of the one-sided traces.
[Thin-interface hypothesis] Suppose that $E,B,D,H$ satisfy the four macroscopic equations of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]] in the distributional sense on $U$ with the source pair $\rho_f=\rho_v+\sigma_f\delta_S$, $J_f=J_v+K_f\delta_S$, where the stationary-sheet pairings are those of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) and the equations are $\operatorname{div}D=\rho_f$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$, $\operatorname{curl}H=J_f+\partial_tD$ as identities in the sense of [[def-distribution]], the fields being identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]) and $\psi$ ranging over $C_c^\infty(U)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). This thin-interface solution hypothesis is a modelling assumption of the statement: it is the natural weakening of the smooth macroscopic equations to fields with a common stationary discontinuity, and it is not deduced from the smooth-region equations alone.
Then, pointwise on $S\times I$, $$n\cdot[D]=\sigma_f,\qquad n\cdot[B]=0,\qquad n\times[E]=0,\qquad n\times[H]=K_f,$$ with the Euclidean inner and cross products of the one-sided traces ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); equivalently $\sigma_f=n\cdot[D]$ and $K_f=n\times[H]$ recover the free sheet densities from the field jumps.
[Weak-trace branch] If instead of the joint extension hypothesis the fields have the original one-sided spatial $C^1$ extensions at each time and, in addition, the piecewise first spatial and temporal derivatives are in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(U)$ and the one-sided field traces are measurable and locally integrable on $S\times I$ with respect to $dS\,dt$, then the same four identities hold as identities of sheet distributions and for $dS\,dt$-almost every $(x,t)$; since the traces are spatially continuous at each fixed time, they hold for every $x\in S$ for almost every $t$, and at every $(x,t)$ whenever the jump densities are additionally jointly continuous. Merely having one-sided spatial $C^1$ traces separately at every time does not justify the last upgrade.
[Scope] In the joint one-sided spacetime $C^1$ extension branch, stationarity and the joint extensions make $\partial_tD$ and $\partial_tB$ locally bounded near $S$ and hence locally integrable, contributing no delta terms. In the weak-trace branch the explicitly assumed locally integrable temporal derivatives provide this conclusion instead. No magnetic charge and no magnetic surface current are present in the sources; no dipolar sheet layer (a concentrated dipole distribution in $P$ or $M$, which would make the fields non-integrable) is included. No existence theorem for fields with singular sources is asserted, no constitutive law is used, and no empirical claim is made.
before.strategy: **Proof technique:** apply [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] to the four fields and match the coefficients of the surface distribution. By [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ declared), for $C^1$-off-$S$ fields with one-sided $C^1$ traces, $\operatorname{div}D=\{\operatorname{div}D\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\cdot[D]\,\delta_S$ and $\operatorname{curl}H=\{\operatorname{curl}H\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\times[H]\,\delta_S$, with the analogous identities for $B$ and $E$. Substituting into the distributional identities of the hypothesis and using the sheet pairings of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c), the regular parts reproduce the off-interface macroscopic equations and the coefficients of $\delta_S$ give, one equation at a time, $n\cdot[D]=\sigma_f$ (from $\operatorname{div}D=\rho_f$), $n\cdot[B]=0$ (from $\operatorname{div}B=0$), $n\times[E]=0$ and $n\times[H]=K_f$: the right-hand sides $\partial_tB$ and $J_f+\partial_tD$ carry no delta term because $S$ is stationary and the joint one-sided $C^1$ hypothesis makes $\partial_tB$ and $\partial_tD$ locally bounded near $S$, hence locally integrable. Since the two-sided traces are continuous on $S\times I$, the distributional coefficient identities are the displayed pointwise identities. The weak-trace branch replaces the pointwise trace argument by the $dS\,dt$-almost-everywhere sheet identity plus the spatial-continuity upgrade. No constitutive relation and no field equation beyond the assumed distributional identities is used.

Then, pointwise on $S\times I$, $$n\cdot[D]=\sigma_f,\qquad n\cdot[B]=0,\qquad n\times[E]=0,\qquad n\times[H]=K_f,$$ with the Euclidean inner and cross products of the one-sided traces ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); equivalently $\sigma_f=n\cdot[D]$ and $K_f=n\times[H]$ recover the free sheet densities from the field jumps.

In the weak-trace branch the explicitly assumed locally integrable temporal derivatives provide this conclusion instead. No magnetic charge and no magnetic surface current are present in the sources; no dipolar sheet layer (a concentrated dipole distribution in $P$ or $M$, which would make the fields non-integrable) is included. before.statement:

abla\chi)$ is a potential pair of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly and its field pair is the field pair of $(\varphi,A)$: $$E(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=E(\varphi,A),\qquad B(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=B(\varphi,A)\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I,$$ the common value being a map $\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly (the field pair of $(\varphi,A)$ in the sense of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]). before.title: Maxwell's equations in potential form: the Lorenz divergence, the decoupled wave equations and residual generators
before.design_state: complete-exact-conditional-research-argument; the exact algebraic identities are stated with their pointwise-regularity hypotheses; solvability is left to the reachability theorem
before.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval, $c>0$, and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ ([[def-em-fields]]) and Lorenz divergence and wave operator $$G:=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi,\qquad W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta.$$ Let $ho:\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R$ and $J:\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R^3$ be continuous sources ([[def-em-sources]]). (a) [Exact identities] Independently of any field equation, on $\Omega	imes I$ $$\operatorname{div}E=W\varphi-\partial_tG,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+
abla G.$$ Consequently the sourced Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold for $(E,B,ho,J)$ if and only if $$W\varphi-\partial_tG= rac{ho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad WA+
abla G=\mu_0J\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I.$$ (b) [Gauge shift] If $\chi$ is a gauge function of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$, then $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G-W\chi$ on $\Omega	imes I$ ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]), and the transformed pair has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). Hence $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge if and only if $W\chi=G$ on $\Omega	imes I$. (c) [Decoupling in Lorenz gauge] Suppose additionally that the given potential pair is in Lorenz gauge, $G=0$ on $\Omega	imes I$. Then its field pair solves the sourced Maxwell system of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] if and only if the pair satisfies the decoupled sourced wave equations
$$W\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad WA=\mu_0J\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I.$$
The source-free equations $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ are automatic for a potential pair. For an arbitrary given $C^2$ potential pair, the conjunction of Lorenz gauge and these wave equations implies the sourced Maxwell system, but Maxwell's equations alone do not impose $G=0$ on that representative. In full generality their exact equivalent conditions remain the residual equations in (a), including $-\partial_tG$ and $
abla G$. Thus the equivalence with decoupled waves holds within the declared Lorenz gauge, without asserting gauge reachability. (d) [Residual generators] If $W\chi=0$ then the transform of a pair in Lorenz gauge is again in Lorenz gauge with the same field pair; the Lorenz condition therefore does not determine the potential pair. (e) [Scope] The identities and equivalences are properties of a given potential representation of class $C^2$; they assert no existence of a generator with $W\chi=G$ (or with prescribed data), which is the subject of the gauge-reachability theorem on this page, and they impose no boundary, decay or initial condition. A pair of class $C^1$ defines $E,B$ but need not have the second derivatives appearing in $W\varphi$, $WA$, $\Delta$ or $\partial_tG$, so $C^2$ is the exact standing regularity here.
before.strategy:
(a) Componentwise expansion using the sum rules for divergence and curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]), the vector identity $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A=
abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A$ for the $C^2$ field $A$ ([[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]]), the definition $\Delta\varphi=\operatorname{div}
abla\varphi$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]) and the equality of mixed partials of the $C^2$ functions $\varphi,A$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]): $\operatorname{div}E=-\Delta\varphi-\partial_t\operatorname{div}A=W\varphi-\partial_tG$, and $\operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=
abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=WA+
abla G$. The two source-free equations hold automatically for a potential pair by [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and [[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]] with the linearity of curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]); hence the equivalence with the sourced system. (b) Direct expansion of $T_\chi$: $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=\operatorname{div}A+\Delta\chi+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi-c^{-2}\partial_t^2\chi=G-W\chi$, using linearity and the $C^2$ mixed-partials identity for $\chi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]); the field part is [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]. (c) Under the explicitly imposed hypothesis $G=0$, the continuously defined derivatives $\partial_tG$ and $
abla G$ vanish. Substitution in (a) turns the two sourced residual equations exactly into $W\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0$ and $WA=\mu_0J$. Conversely those two wave equations with $G=0$ make the residual equations hold, and the two source-free equations were already proved for every potential pair. There is no inference from Maxwell alone to a gauge condition; (d) is (b) with $G=0$ and $W\chi=0$. No choice principle, no hypothesis on the shape of $\Omega$ and no solvability of $W\chi=G$ is used.

before.title: Rectangular PEC guide and cavity geometry, the zero-normal-B reflection class, and axis-relative TE/TM/TEM
before.statement:
Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, its SI units and its fields $E,B$ be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]] and [[def-em-fields]]. Fix $a,b>0$, write $x_t=(x_1,x_2)$, $e_z:=e_3$, and define $\nabla_t f=(\partial_1f,\partial_2f,0)$, $\Delta_t f=\partial_1^2f+\partial_2^2f$ and $\operatorname{div}_tu_t=\partial_1u_1+\partial_2u_2$ for the stated regularity, using [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]].
(a) [Straight guide] A straight guide region is $\Omega_A:=A\times\mathbb R$ where $A$ is either a bounded connected $C^1$ plane domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]) or the explicit rectangular cross-section; the rectangle has corners and is treated by its open faces, not asserted to be a $C^1$ boundary domain, with longitudinal axis $e_z$; for a rectangular cross-section $A=R_{ab}:=(0,a)\times(0,b)$ the region is called the rectangular guide and its walls are the four open faces $\{x_1=0\},\{x_1=a\},\{x_2=0\},\{x_2=b\}$. A rectangular cavity region is $\Omega_c:=(0,a)\times(0,b)\times(0,d)$ for fixed $d>0$, with the six open faces as its walls. The separate smooth-cavity spectral branch uses an explicitly declared bounded $C^\infty$ domain in $\mathbb R^3$ with its smooth PEC boundary; it is not the rectangular reflection class. Spatial derivatives are taken at fixed $t$; the fields are defined on $\Omega\times I$ with the regularity declared by each theorem.
(b) [PEC boundary model] On every open wall (a wall minus its edges) the ideal perfectly conducting boundary model declares the two conditions $n\times E=0$ and $n\cdot B=0$, where $n$ is the outward unit normal of that wall ($-e_1,+e_1,-e_2,+e_2$ on the four rectangular walls, and $\pm e_j$ on the six cavity walls). Its physical reading is the ideal-conductor limit of the stationary interface conditions of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]]: with $E=B=0$ inside the ideal conductor the tangential electric field and the normal magnetic field vanish, while the surface-charge and surface-current readings $n\cdot D=\sigma_f$ and $n\times H=K_f$ are determined by the traces and are not prescribed here. The supplier's hypotheses (a compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with one-sided $C^1$ fields) cover a smooth stationary interface, not the $\sigma\to\infty$ idealization nor the box edges; the guide/cavity conditions on the open walls are therefore declared as an idealization of this definition, and no pointwise statement on the edges is made.
(c) [Zero-normal-B reflection class] For the rectangular box $Q=\prod_{j=1}^3(0,L_j)$ with $L=(a,b,d)$, the reflection class is the class of locally integrable fields $E,B$ on $Q$ whose extensions to the rectangular torus $\prod_j\mathbb R/(2L_j\mathbb Z)$, defined by extending $E_1$ evenly across the $x_1$-walls and oddly across the $x_2$-, $x_3$-walls and cyclically for $E_2,E_3$, and extending $B_1$ oddly across $x_1$ and evenly across $x_2,x_3$ and cyclically for $B_2,B_3$, are $L^2$ fields, together with the distributional constraints that $\operatorname{div}E$ and $\operatorname{div}B$ vanish on the torus for the extensions. This is the declared weak PEC model used for the cavity initial-value problem; for smooth fields the parities give $n\times E=0$ and $n\cdot B=0$ on $\partial Q$. Initial data not in this class (for example data with trapped normal $B$) are excluded, as are the general $H(\operatorname{curl})$ boundary classes, which are defined by the mathematical suppliers and are not identified here with the classical conditions.
(d) [TE, TM, TEM] For a guide or cavity field $(E,B)$, the longitudinal components are $E_z:=E\cdot e_z$ and $B_z:=B\cdot e_z$; the field is called TE (transverse electric) if $E_z\equiv0$, TM (transverse magnetic) if $B_z\equiv0$, and TEM if both vanish, always relative to the named axis $e_z$.
(e) [Separated phasor convention] For $\omega>0$ and $\beta\in\mathbb C$, a $\beta$-$\omega$ separated phasor field on the guide is a real field of the form $F(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\tilde F(x_1,x_2)e^{i(\beta x_3-\omega t)}\bigr)$ with a complex amplitude $\tilde F$, componentwise; $\omega/(2\pi)$ is the frequency and $\beta$ the longitudinal propagation constant; when $\beta$ is real, $\beta>0$ describes propagation in the $+e_z$ direction under this phase convention, while a complex $\beta$ gives the spatial factor $e^{-\operatorname{Im}\beta x_3}$ and may grow in the opposite direction; each consuming branch states its selection.
(f) [Scope] The definition fixes the geometry, the PEC boundary model, the weak reflection class and the mode terminology; it asserts no field equation, no constitutive law and no existence or completeness of modes, Rectangular TE/TM candidates and the rectangular reflection class, declared smooth bounded PEC cavity spectral classes, and smooth straight-guide TEM potential branches (including the coaxial annulus) are within this geometry. No general non-rectangular TE/TM guide theory, circular-guide spectral classification, open-end or junction scattering, or lossy model is supplied.
before.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition: geometry and transversality are fixed by coordinates and normals; the PEC model is declared with its interface reading and its excluded idealization/edges; the reflection class is defined by the reflection rules and distributional divergence constraints; the phasor convention is stated as an encoding of real fields. No differential equation is introduced.
before.physical_scope: The ideal PEC boundary model of the straight rectangular guide and cavity (and of straight guides with a bounded connected C1 cross-section) in the lossless laboratory chart, together with the zero-normal-B reflection class and the TE/TM/TEM classification. The boundary model is an idealization of an interface with a perfectly conducting medium on the open walls; the definition asserts no field equations, constitutive laws or mode completeness.

before.title: The uniformly charged ball: interior and exterior fields, continuous potential and finite energy
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the cited Lebesgue, polar, Newtonian and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $a>0$, $Q\in\mathbb R$, let $\overline B_a=\{x:|x|\le a\}$ ([[def-metric-ball]]), and define, with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] ([[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-sources]]),
$$\rho(x):=\frac{3Q}{4\pi a^3}\,\mathbf 1_{\{|x|<a\}}(x),\qquad
E(x):=\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\begin{cases}x/a^3,&|x|<a,\\ x/|x|^3,&|x|\ge a,\end{cases}\qquad
\varphi(x):=\begin{cases}\dfrac{Q(3a^2-|x|^2)}{8\pi\varepsilon_0a^3},&|x|\le a,\\[6pt]\dfrac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0|x|},&|x|\ge a.\end{cases}$$
(The value of $\rho$ on the sphere $\{|x|=a\}$ is immaterial: it is a Lebesgue-null set by the polar calculation $\lambda_3(S_a)=4\pi\int_0^\infty\mathbf1_{\{a\}}(r)r^2dr=0$, since the one-dimensional singleton has measure zero ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]], [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]]).) Then:
(a) [Regularity and gradient] $E$ is continuous on $\mathbb R^3$, of class $C^\infty$ on each of the open regions $\{|x|<a\}$, $\{|x|>a\}$; $\varphi\in C^1(\mathbb R^3)$, its displayed branch derivatives agree on $\{|x|=a\}$, and $E=-\nabla\varphi$ on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]);
(b) [Classical equations] for every $x$ with $|x|\ne a$,
$$\operatorname{div}E(x)=\rho(x)/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E(x)=0$$
([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]);
(c) [Weak equations] the pair $(E,(\rho,0))$ satisfies the spatial distributional equations $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$: $E$ is $C^1$ on each side of the sphere $S_a=\{|x|=a\}$ with one-sided continuous traces that agree, $[E]=0$, so [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] gives
$$\operatorname{div}E=\{\operatorname{div}E\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\cdot[E]\,\delta_{S_a}=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=\{\operatorname{curl}E\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\times[E]\,\delta_{S_a}=0,$$
with $\rho$ the displayed locally integrable density and no surface-charge term ([[def-em-weak-sources]], [[lem-em-euclidean-balls-and-annuli-are-bounded-c-one-domains]] for the sphere as a compact embedded smooth hypersurface); by the fixed-time reading of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e) these are the weak equations of the static model for this source, with zero singular part;
(d) [Energy] the field energy is finite and equals the assembly integral,
$$\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|E|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\varphi\,d\lambda_3=\frac{3Q^2}{20\pi\varepsilon_0a},$$
computed with the polar formula ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]]); the value agrees with the smooth-source identity of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]] although the density here is only piecewise continuous;
(e) [Consistency and contrast] for $|x|>a$ the field is exactly the point-charge Coulomb field of total charge $Q$ centred at the origin ([[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (d) with $x_0=0$) although the source is the extended ball, and for $|x|<a$ it is the affine field $Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3)$; $\varphi$ is continuous at $|x|=a$ and decays at infinity; the field is bounded on $\mathbb R^3$, so no divergence of field energy occurs for the extended source;
(f) [Scope] the example verifies the displayed candidate and its energy; it does not claim uniqueness of the solution (this would require boundary data and an infinity condition, and the density is not continuous), it asserts no empirical content, and the density $\rho$ is treated as a bounded $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ density with the sphere carrying no surface charge ($[E]=0$).
before.strategy:
For (a): on $\{|x|<a\}$, $E$ is the affine map $Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3)$ and on $\{|x|>a\}$ it is $Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^3)$; both are $C^\infty$ on their open domains ([[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). At $|x|=a$ the two formulas coincide ($x/a^3=x/a^3$), so $E$ is continuous on all of $\mathbb R^3$ ([[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]], [[def-metric-ball]]). For $\varphi$, the interior branch has gradient $-Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3)$ and the exterior branch has gradient $-Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^3)$ by the chain rule, and the two gradients agree on $\{|x|=a\}$; the matching derivatives also exist on the interface, as follows. Let $F(r)$ be the displayed radial potential profile on $r\ge0$. Its two branches agree at $a$, and their one-sided derivatives both equal $-Q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^2)$, so the difference quotient $(F(a+h)-F(a))/h$ has that common limit from either sign. Thus $F$ is differentiable at $a$, and its derivative is continuous there by the branch formulas. Since $x\mapsto|x|$ is differentiable near each point of $S_a$, the chain rule proves actual total differentiability of $\varphi=F(|x|)$ there and gives the matching gradient. At the origin the interior polynomial already gives smoothness. The resulting partial derivatives exist and are continuous everywhere, whence $\varphi$ is $C^1$ with $\nabla\varphi=-E$ ([[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).
For (b): inside, $\operatorname{div}(Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3))=3Q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3)=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and the curl of an affine field vanishes ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]); outside, $\operatorname{div}(Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^3))=\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_i\partial_i(x_i|x|^{-3})=\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}(3|x|^{-3}-3|x|^{-3})=0$ and the curl components $\partial_j(x_k|x|^{-3})-\partial_k(x_j|x|^{-3})=0$ vanish by the same direct differentiation ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]), matching $\rho=0$ outside.
For (c): the set $S_a$ is a compact embedded smooth hypersurface with unit normal $n=x/|x|$, and the two sides $\Omega_-=\{|x|<a\}$, $\Omega_+=\{|x|>a\}$ are open; $E$ is $C^1$ on each side and its one-sided traces agree on $S_a$ (from (a)), so $[E]=F_+-F_-=0$ in the notation of [[def-em-surface-distribution]] and [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] applies: the distributional divergence is the piecewise classical divergence plus $n\cdot[E]\delta_{S_a}=0$, and the distributional curl is the piecewise classical curl plus $n\times[E]\delta_{S_a}=0$. By (b) the piecewise divergence is $\rho/\varepsilon_0$ as a locally integrable function and the piecewise curl is $0$; the sphere is null by applying [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]] to its Borel indicator: $\lambda_3(S_a)=4\pi\int_0^\infty\mathbf1_{\{a\}}(r)r^2dr=0$. A singleton is contained in intervals of arbitrarily small length, so its one-dimensional measure is zero; [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]] then applies, and the pairing conventions are those of [[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]] and [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]. The static reading is [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e), and the source objects are those of [[def-em-weak-sources]] with zero singular part.
For (d): by the polar formula and $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]]) one has $\int_{B_a}|x|^2\,d\lambda_3=4\pi\int_0^ar^4\,dr=\frac{4\pi a^5}{5}$ and $\int_{B_a}d\lambda_3=\frac{4\pi a^3}{3}$; hence
$$\int_{B_a}|E|^2=\Bigl(\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3}\Bigr)^2\frac{4\pi a^5}{5}=\frac{Q^2}{20\pi\varepsilon_0^2a},\qquad \int_{|x|>a}|E|^2=\frac{Q^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2}\cdot 4\pi\int_a^\infty r^{-2}dr=\frac{Q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0^2a},$$
using $\int_a^\infty r^{-2}dr=1/a$ ([[thm-ftc-second-part]] and monotone convergence, [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]); the sum times $\varepsilon_0/2$ is $\frac{Q^2}{40\pi\varepsilon_0a}+\frac{Q^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0a}=\frac{3Q^2}{20\pi\varepsilon_0a}$. The assembly integral is computed from the same two radial integrals, $\frac12\int\rho\varphi=\frac12\frac{3Q}{4\pi a^3}\frac{Q}{8\pi\varepsilon_0a^3}\bigl(3a^2\frac{4\pi a^3}{3}-\frac{4\pi a^5}{5}\bigr)=\frac{3Q^2}{20\pi\varepsilon_0a}$, so the identity of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]] extends to this piecewise-continuous bounded density by direct verification; the density is bounded with compact support and all integrands are continuous off a null sphere ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]]).
For (e): the exterior branch equals the formula of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (d) with $q=Q$, $x_0=0$; $\varphi$ is continuous at $|x|=a$ since both branches give $Q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a)$, and decays like $1/|x|$; $|E|\le |Q|/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^2)$ on $\mathbb R^3$, so the energy of (d) is finite and no point singularity arises. For (f): no uniqueness or empirical statement is used anywhere; the sphere's zero jump is exactly the checked equality of the two branches on $\{|x|=a\}$. The one-dimensional singleton used in the polar null-sphere calculation is null by [[prop-degenerate-boxes-and-coordinate-hyperplanes-are-lebesgue-null]]. Finite-interval integrations of the continuous one-variable test/radial integrands above use [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] to identify their Riemann/FTC values with their Lebesgue values before Fubini, polar integration or passage to improper limits; real and imaginary test components are treated separately.
